title: UK Sex Workers Wake Up to Sites Purging Their Content Following Porn Ban
content:
Immediately after the UK banned a wide range of porn fantasies involving choking, breath-restriction, and relative roleplay, adult creators watched platforms remove hundreds of their videos — even when the creators thought they were in compliance with the law. These creators say they were blindsided by the removals, since the content didn’t seem to violate the law at all.

Creators are reporting one platform in particular, Clips4Sale, is purging content with little notice, “a precautionary measure.”   

Some creators who’ve contacted Clips4Sale to appeal these removals have shared screenshots online of the reply the platform sends: “At this time, we have implemented a general restriction on content availability in the UK to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements,” Clips4Sale support replies, according to these screenshots, viewed by 404 Media. “This is a precautionary measure and does not necessarily indicate that your clips contain prohibited content or violate our policies. We are continuing to review affected content, and additional clips will be made available to UK buyers as they are reviewed and cleared.”

title: EU: Commission’s findings on TikTok “rabbit hole” effect must trigger fundamental changes to social media design
content:
Responding to the European Commission’s preliminary findings that TikTok is in breach of the Digital Services Act (DSA) because of the “rabbit hole” effect of its recommender system, Lisa Dittmer, Amnesty International Researcher on Children and Young People’s Digital Rights, said:    

“The Commission’s preliminary finding that TikTok’s ‘For You’ feed puts users’ wellbeing at risk is a welcome and urgently needed step in the fight for accountability and safer online platforms. Amnesty International’s research has repeatedly documented how TikTok draws some children into rabbit holes of depressive and suicidal ideation content. Young people and bereaved parents shared with us how TikTok’s feed normalized and exacerbated teenagers’ struggles with depression and self-harm. This should never have been allowed to happen.

title: Analysis: China’s quarterly CO2 falls 3% in largest drop since Covid
content:
China’s carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions fell by 3.1% in the third quarter of 2026, as the Hormuz crisis continued to hit oil demand and coal use also dropped.

Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air

This was the largest quarterly reduction since the 2022 Covid lockdowns and means that China’s CO2 emissions have now fallen by an estimated 0.5% in the year to date.

The new analysis for Carbon Brief, based on official figures and commercial data, shows that coal use fell by 3% year-on-year in the third quarter of 2026, while oil was down 4%.

The main drivers were a fall in power-sector coal consumption, a continued sharp reduction in transport oil consumption and slowing growth in the coal-to-chemical industry.

The sharp decline in China’s CO2 emissions extends a “flat or falling” trend that began in March 2024 and has now lasted more than two years, as shown in the figure below.

The outlook for China’s CO2 emissions depends on the balance between rising energy demand, clean-energy growth and the government response to a GDP slowdown.

title: National Politics Will Never Be the Same: Juan González on How Latino Voters Remade the Political Map
content:
The midterms saw a landslide of Latinos vote for Democrats. In Texas, California, Kansas and Colorado, Latinos who had voted for Republicans just two years ago voted for Democrats in large numbers, helping secure Democratic control of both the House and the Senate. Latino lawmakers will make up about a fifth of the Democratic majority in the House. And in an historic victory, the two most populous states in the country, California and Texas, will soon be led by Democratic Latino governors.

“Texas has been suddenly transformed into a battleground state,” says Democracy Now! co-host Juan Gonzalez. “Texas has been the biggest and most important red state in the country for decades, and I’ve been predicting for years that it is the key link for achieving a realignment of national politics.”

title: Presenting 'Desire Lines: Encoding Queer Digital Futures'
content:
What does the digital future look like? Who gets to imagine it, shape it, and make it real?

Building a freer, more inclusive digital age requires not only challenging systems of surveillance and control, but also making space for creativity, community, and radical imagination. 

That's why earlier this year with the queer arts collective, we put out a call for submissions inviting people to explore the intersections of technology, identity, and digital liberation—whether that involved pointing the lens towards an underrepresented issue in digital justice efforts; sharing personal accounts of joy, pleasure, or sorrow under surveillance; or painting wide imaginations for our communities using technology for good instead of carcerality and doom.

And we’re excited to share that the project is now live! Desire Lines: Encoding Queer Digital Futures explores a digital world that dreams wilder and exists louder. Seven artists share their visions of digital liberation, spanning from early internet-coded yearning to escapist steamy chat rooms and seed-laced battle suits for revolution.

title: January 2026 Protests: Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divband Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, the Revolutionary Court has sentenced Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divband, two protesters held in Karaj Central Prison, to death.

Based on information obtained by HRANA, the two men were sentenced to death by Branch 2 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Sabzevari, in a case related to the January 2026 protests. The sentences were issued on the charge of “operational action,” with the court citing provisions concerning the intensification of punishments under the Islamic Penal Code.

Hamid Kazemi and Hassan Divband were arrested by security forces during the nationwide protests last winter and subsequently transferred to Karaj Central Prison.

HRANA’s investigation into the specific allegations against the two men and the latest developments in their legal cases remains ongoing.

title: Terveet eläimet ja puhdas ruoka ovat tulevaisuuden turva – Eläinlääkäriliiton eduskuntavaalitavoitteet 2027
content:
Muuttuvassa maailmassa suomalaisten turva on korkeatasoinen eläinlääkintähuolto ja terveysriskien tehokas valvonta. Eläinlääkärien toimintaedellytyksiä on parannettava, jotta globaaleja terveysuhkia pystytään torjumaan tulevaisuudessakin.

– Turvaamalla ympäristöterveydenhuollon henkilöstöresurssit suojaamme ihmisiä terveysriskeiltä, joita liittyy esimerkiksi ruokaan, uimaveteen ja luonnonvaraisiin eläimiin. Ruokamyrkytysepidemiat ja viimeisimpänä afrikkalaisen sikaruton leviäminen sekä siitä seuranneet rajoitustoimet osoittavat, miten terveysriskit voivat näkyä suomalaisten arjessa, sanoo Eläinlääkäriliiton puheenjohtaja Mikko Turku.

Suomessa eläimet ovat terveitä, ruoka ja vesi puhtaita, antibiootit tehoavat eikä ihmisten tarvitse pelätä eläimistä tarttuvia tauteja. Tilanne on kansainvälisesti vertailtuna erinomainen, mutta sen säilyttäminen edellyttää eläinten ja elintarvikkeiden tehokasta valvontaa.

title: Omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua voi hakea nyt verkossa koko Pohjois-Savossa
content:
Pohjois-Savon hyvinvointialue on laajentanut sosiaalipalvelujen digitaalista asiointia ikääntyneille suunnattuihin palveluihin. OmaSavossa voi nyt hakea sähköisesti omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua.

- Omaishoidon tuen ja kuljetuspalvelun hakeminen onnistuu silloin, kun asiakkaalle tai läheiselle parhaiten sopii. Digitaalisesti täytetty hakemus siirtyy suoraan ammattilaisen käsittelyyn, asiakasohjauksen palveluyksikköjohtaja Hanna Jokinen kuvaa.

Hyvinvointialueella on tällä hetkellä noin 1 650 omaishoidon tuen saajaa. Vuonna 2025 uusia omaishoidon tuen saajia tuli 413, ja tämän vuoden arvio on noin 430.

Asiakas voi täyttää OmaSavossa esimerkiksi iäkkäiden palvelujen hakemuksen, jolla voi hakea omaishoidon tukea ja kuljetuspalvelua. Hakemus siirtyy OmaSavosta suoraan ammattilaisen käsittelyyn.

Kun päätös on tehty, asiakas voi lukea sen OmaKannasta ja Suomi.fi-viestit-palvelusta. Jos asiakas ei ole ottanut Suomi.fi-viestejä käyttöön, hän saa päätöksen paperipostilla.

Ikäkeskuksen neuvontaan tulee kuukausittain keskimäärin 1 300–1 400 yhteydenottoa, joista 75 prosenttia on puhelinsoittoja.

title: Tanzanian Court Convicts Opposition Leader of Incitement
content:
Tanzania’s High Court on November 6 convicted Tundu Lissu, the leader of Tanzania’s main opposition party, Chama Cha Demokrasia Na Maendeleo (the ‘Party of Democracy and Development’, or CHADEMA), of incitement, sentencing him to four years in prison. The judges acquitted him of treason, a charge that carries the death penalty.

Authorities accused him of having planned to instigate the public to obstruct the October 2025 elections, based on remarks he made at an April 3, 2025, rally in Dar es Salaam. CHADEMA had been calling for the government to undertake “fundamental electoral reforms” as part of its campaign, “No Reforms, No Elections.” Prior to his conviction, Lissu had been imprisoned without bail since his April 9, 2025 arrest.

The proceedings against Lissu raised serious human rights concerns. His trial faced repeated delays, and he represented himself after saying the authorities had denied him private access to his lawyers.

title: EU accuses TikTok of designing algorithm that creates ‘rabbit holes’
content:
The European Commission has accused TikTok of violating its online platforms rules for having designed algorithms that lead users down so-called rabbit holes.

The preliminary findings announced Friday mark the first time the Commission has focused on a social media platform’s recommender systems as a breach of its powerful Digital Services Act, under which it can issue fines up to 6% of a company’s annual global revenue.

“This is the first time that we are really tackling head-on the engagement-based recommender system model,” said one Commission official, who was granted speaking anonymity to speak freely.

This is the fifth case of the EU executive accusing TikTok of breaching EU rules, even though it has issued no fines against the Chinese-owned platform.

In Friday’s announcement, the Commission says the company didn’t adequately consider the risk of sending users down “rabbit holes” through a “continuous stream of personalised videos, even when those are related to mental health struggles and body image.”

The investigation focused on mental health impacts because “the evidence was strongest,” when asked about how these rabbit holes contribute to radicalization, said another official.

title: Ulkoministeri Valtonen Varsovaan
content:
Ulkoministeri Valtonen osallistuu 6. marraskuuta Itämeren valtioiden neuvoston (Council of the Baltic Sea States, CBSS) ja Ukrainan epäviralliseen ministeritapaamiseen Varsovassa, Puolassa.

Tapaamisessa ulkoministerit keskustelevat Ukrainan rauhanprosessista ja Ukrainan tukemisesta sekä vastaamisesta Venäjän hybriditoimiin.

”Keskustelemme läheisten liittolaisten ja kumppanien kanssa Ukrainan rauhanprosessista, jonka rinnalla on yhä tärkeää jatkaa vahvaa tukeamme Ukrainalle erityisesti talven lähestyessä sekä lisätä painetta Venäjälle. Varsovassa kokoontuvilla Itämeren alueen mailla on tässä tärkeä rooli”, ulkoministeri Valtonen sanoo.

title: In Conversation with Benedeck Jávor, Hungary
content:
Benedek Jávor is a Hungarian Green activist and politician. Originally a biologist, he was an environmental campaigner before entering politics, founding and leading a major green NGO in Hungary. In 2009, he co-founded the first Hungarian Green Party, Politics Can Be Different (LMP), which entered the country’s parliament the following year. He served a four-year mandate as a member of parliament. In 2014, he was elected to the European Parliament, on behalf of a newly created Green Party – Dialogue for Hungary (PM). He currently heads the representation office of the city of Budapest to the EU.

In this interview Benedek Jávor traces the development of Hungary’s Green politics over the past decades, from its emergence out of grassroots environmental struggles, to the ideological divisions that lead to a fundamental schism, and the destructive impact of the Orbán years on a promising political movement that was just beginning to bear fruit.

Can you tell us about the origins of the ecological movement in Hungary, particularly around the end of the communist era?

title: The Cop31 climate summit is betting on electrification – but still needs a plan to ditch fossil fuels
content:
The latest UN climate summit, Cop31, will get underway in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9. One of its key objectives is to boost electrification across the global economy – replacing petrol and diesel vehicles, gas boilers and some industrial processes that burn fossil fuels with electric alternatives.

The summit’s host, Turkey, has set a target of 35% of energy demand being met by electricity by 2035, up from around 20% today. Announcing the “35-by-35” pledge, Cop31 president Murat Kurum described it as “one of the defining features” of Turkey’s presidency, highlighting the risks of continued dependence on imported fossil fuels.

Without doubt, electrification is essential to curtailing greenhouse gas emissions, and is already gathering pace. The International Energy Agency (IEA) has declared we are living in the “age of electricity”, and if stated policy pledges hold, global electrification rates will hit 31% by 2050. The Cop31’s focus on electrification hopes to build upon and accelerate this existing trend.

title: Loputon Eurooppa
content:
The Ulkopolitist ja Eurooppanuoret järjestivät syksyllä 2026 Eurooppa ja eurooppalaisuus -teemaisen kirjoituskilpailun 14-19 -vuotiaille nuorille. Lily Fu voitti kilpailussa toisen sijan.

Mietin usein saksalaisen elektronisen musiikin yhtyeen Kraftwerkin vuonna 1977 julkaisemaa kappaletta ”Europa Endlos”. Kappaleessa toistettu tyyni ilmaus ”Elämä on ajaton / Eurooppa on loputon” luo hypnoottisen kuvan rajattomasta, muuttumattomasta ja yhtenäisestä Euroopasta. Kappaleen luoma kuva on täynnä vanhan maailman romantiikkaa: hotelleja, puistoja, palatseja ja bulevardeja, mutta samalla tämän pintakiillon alla sykkivät haikeus ja yksinäisyys. Ikään kuin matkustaja katsoisi junan ikkunasta ulos ja näkisi sodan kokeneen ja hieman rappeutuneen Euroopan maisemien vilisevän ohi.

title: ”Lopettakaa sodat. Lopettakaa naisten, tyttöjen ja kaikkien siviilien tappaminen.” – UN Womenin apulaispääjohtaja Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvandan puhe YK:n pääsihteerin Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuusraportin julkistamistilaisuudessa
content:
Ennen kuin aloitan, haluan kunnioittaa sodissa henkensä menettäneiden muistoa. Niiden naisten, miesten, tyttöjen ja poikien muistoa, joilta riistettiin tulevaisuus. Ja omien kollegoidemme muistoa – niiden, jotka menettivät henkensä yrittäessään pelastaa muita.

Joka päivä sota ja väkivalta avautuvat silmiemme edessä.

Puhelimissamme. Televisioruuduillamme. Loputtomana kuvavirtana tuhoutuneista kodeista, surevista äideistä, haavoittuneista lapsista ja perheistä, jotka pakenevat henkensä edestä.

Me näemme kaiken tämän. Emmekä silti näe koko kuvaa.

Tänään julkaistava YK:n pääsihteerin Naiset, rauha ja turvallisuus -raportti tuo näiden kuvien rinnalle tutkittua tietoa ja pakottaa meidät kohtaamaan järkyttävän todellisuuden:

Sodista on tulossa yhä tappavampia naisille ja tytöille. Ja maailma antaa sen tapahtua.

Tällä hetkellä yli 750 miljoonaa naista ja tyttöä elää alle 50 kilometrin päässä aktiivisesta konfliktialueesta. Heille sota ei ole jotakin, jonka ohi voi vain selata puhelimellaan. Sota on heidän kotiovellaan.

Sota seuraa naisia synnytysosastoille. Koululuokkiin. Keittiöihin. Paikkoihin, joissa perheiden pitäisi voida olla turvassa.

title: Polaaripyörre on hajonnut harvinaisen aikaisin – tätä on ehkä luvassa
content:
Napa-alueita kiertävä polaaripyörre on hajonnut harvinaisen aikaisin. Yleensä hajoaminen on keskitalven ilmiö, kertoi Ilmatieteen laitoksen päivystävä meteorologi Heikki Sinisalo STT:lle perjantaina.

Vaikutukset säähän näkyvät kuitenkin vasta viikkojen päästä. Varmuudella Sinisalo ei osaa sanoa, millaisia vaikutukset ovat ja missä vaiheessa ne tapahtuvat.

Yleensä polaaripyörteen hajoaminen tuo mukanaan kylmää ilmaa arktisten alueiden yltä. Yllättäen yhdessä yössä muutos ei kuitenkaan tapahdu, vaan kylmän ilman saapuminen näkyy ennusteissa, Sinisalo kertoo.

Polaaripyörre on laaja matalapaine ja kylmän ilman alue napa-alueiden yläpuolella stratosfäärissä. Jos polaaripyörre hajoaa, pääsee kylmää ilmaa virtaamaan napa-alueilta kohti eteläisempiä leveysasteita.

Polaaripyörteen hajoamisesta kertoi aiemmin Ilta-Sanomat.

title: Tanzania: Conviction and sentencing of opposition leader Tundu Lissu a travesty of justice
content:
Reacting to Friday’s conviction of Tanzanian opposition leader Tundu Lissu and his sentence of four years’ imprisonment for incitement, after he was acquitted of treason, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for East and Southern Africa, Tigere Chagutah, said:

“Tundu Lissu should never have been arrested, let alone prosecuted and convicted. Today’s verdict and four-year prison sentence are the culmination of a deeply flawed process that was unjust from the moment of his arrest. He has already spent 577 days in arbitrary detention solely for the peaceful exercise of his human rights.

title: Purple Mississippi? Overcoming GOP Voter Suppression, Black Voters Power Dem Wins Across the South
content:
Mississippi’s race for the U.S. Senate remains too close to call: Democrat Scott Colom is narrowly leading Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith by nearly 2,000 votes with 96% of votes counted as of Friday morning. Donald Trump carried Mississippi by 23 points in 2024. If elected, Colom would be the first Democrat to win the state in 40 years and the first African American since 1875, during the Reconstruction era. Colom, the former district attorney for northeast Mississippi, made the issue of affordability central to his campaign. He has sharply criticized national Democrats for writing off Mississippi and failing to invest in his campaign early on.

“The entire country shifted left. But when you look at it regionally, the biggest shifts took place in the South — Texas, Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana,” says Cliff Albright, executive director of Black Voters Matter. That “wave of energy” was “largely led by Black voters who were most under attack with the mid-decade racial gerrymandering that was taking place. It clearly backfired, and all it did was to wake up a sleeping giant.”

title: EFF Submission to OHCHR Consultation on Child Rights and Safety in the Digital Environment
content:
“The safety of young people in the digital environment cannot be assessed without also considering the safety of young people in offline environments. For millions of young people around the world, the digital environment is their safe place, their haven from an unsafe physical environment, community, or family situation. The digital environment may be the best, perhaps only, place for them to find critical safety information and community, to explore ideas that are controversial in their families and larger physical environments, and to otherwise nourish their personal autonomy.

“For these young people, regulatory efforts that limit their access to online services or to certain features they find valuable, make their lives, in total, less safe, even if there has been some marginal safety benefit to their digital environment.

“The OHCHR must thus consider the whole of young persons' lives in any recommendations that come out of this process and not treat ‘safety, physical or mental health, and rights in the digital environment’ as disconnected from safety, physical or mental health, and rights elsewhere.”

title: A New Chapter for Corporate Accountability in the UK and the Road Ahead
content:
The government announced on November 4 that it will propose a law regulating the human rights impacts of companies in the United Kingdom’s global supply chain. The UK’s Corporate Justice Coalition, along with some businesses, have long led advocacy efforts for such legislation. The government’s announcement responds to some of those demands and marks a chance to turn corporate responsibility into meaningful legal obligations.

According to the announcement, the largest businesses operating in the UK would be required to identify, assess, and address human rights abuses and labor exploitation in their operations and supply chains. Regulators would also be empowered to investigate goods suspected of being made with forced labor and, when companies have failed to meet their obligations, order their removal from the British market.

If designed and implemented effectively, these measures could make a real difference to workers. 

But the opportunity extends beyond labor rights. 

Human rights and environmental harm are deeply interconnected. The UK should build on its announcement by extending mandatory due diligence to environmental and climate-related human rights risks.

title: Working in Groups: Start Here
content:
Welcome to the Working in Groups topic in the Commons Social Change Library. Effective and lasting change tends to be the result of people working together in groups and networks towards a shared goal. Social change can’t be won by isolated individuals, it requires us to do the rewarding but sometimes messy work of collaborating with others.

This topic is designed to offer a range of resources to help organisations and individuals be more informed, intentional and skilled when engaging in group work.

For groups to work effectively there needs to be a level of coordination, collaboration, promotion of diversity, and the skills to participate and facilitate well. Conflict and power dynamics are inherent parts of group life that can be understood, prepared for and responded to. Team work and morale can be fostered and built.

You can search within the topic by using the ‘Refine by Format’, ‘Refine by Author’, and ‘Refine by Collection’ filter functions. The ‘Refine by Topic’ option will assist in applying a filter that will identify resources which cross over with other topics within the Commons Social Change Library (e.g. Diversity & Inclusion).

title: The Greens Hit 50
content:
The 2020s are a pivotal decade, both for the Greens and the world at large. The Greens really began to feel their feet in the 1990s and early 2000s, back when the “end of history” promise of progress was the spirit of the times. What succeeded it has been at least a decade and a half of disorder. Liberal democracy’s struggle to grapple with populism and right-wing authoritarianism, profound technological change, and growing environmental crisis to which the uncertain energy transition is only a partial answer are central elements of this new disorder. 

This same context is also the backdrop for green politics in Europe gaining more political power than ever before. Energised by the global climate awakening, Green parties entered government in 7 EU countries between 2018 and 2021. Their surge pushed the European Commission to put forward its European Green Deal, an ambitious regulatory agenda centred on reaching “net zero” carbon emissions by 2050.

title: Justice, accountability, more questions: what Russell Brand’s guilty verdict means for victim-survivors
content:
British comedian and actor Russell Brand has been found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault, related to multiple victims, after a four-week trial in London.

He was acquitted on three other charges.

The offences for which Brand was convicted occurred nearly two decades ago.

Meanwhile, United Kingdom police are investigating further allegations of rape made by two other women.

For the six women who came forward to report their experiences, the verdict marks the culmination of a long and undoubtedly difficult journey through the criminal legal system.

Much of the public attention will now likely turn to Brand himself: his sentence, his public reputation and whether he will seek to appeal.

But we should also be asking what this verdict means for victim-survivors of sexual violence.

Though the Brand case occurred in the UK, the rates of sexual violence and trends in justice outcomes are very similar there as they are in Australia. Unfortunately, when we examine those trends, we see justice in response to sexual violence is incredibly rare.

title: Eurooppalaisuus on päätös
content:
The Ulkopolitist ja Eurooppanuoret järjestivät syksyllä 2026 Eurooppa ja eurooppalaisuus -teemaisen kirjoituskilpailun 14-19 -vuotiaille nuorille. Greta Lindroos voitti kilpailussa kolmannen sijan.

Kun ajattelen Eurooppaa, en ensimmäisenä ajattele sinistä lippua ja kahtatoista tähteä. Ajattelen maailmaa, jossa olen saanut kasvaa ilman, että olen joutunut miettimään, minkä maan raja tulee seuraavaksi vastaan. Voin kuunnella ranskalaista artistia, katsoa espanjalaista sarjaa, keskustella virolaisen nuoren kanssa tai matkustaa toiseen Euroopan maahan ilman, että minun tarvitsee tiedostaa kansallisuuttani jatkuvasti.

Ehkä juuri rajattomuus ja vapaus saavat Euroopan merkityksen helposti unohtumaan. Eurooppalaisuus tuntuu joskus niin tavalliselta, ettei sen poikkeuksellisuutta huomaa. Se on ajatus siitä, että erilaiset kielet, kulttuurit, uskonnot ja historiat voivat olla olemassa samaan aikaan ilman, että yhden täytyy voittaa ja muiden kadota.

title: When the Watchdogs Are Silenced: India's Crackdown on Those Documenting Online Censorship
content:
On November 3, our colleagues at the Software Freedom Law Center, India (SFLC.in) received notifications from X that the Delhi Police had issued takedown requests targeting 42 URLs. Among the accounts and posts targeted were those belonging to SFLC.in, the Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF), and X account @geoblockedindia, as well as posts documenting legal notices and instances of online censorship. 

Takedown requests targeting SFLC.in and other digital rights groups threaten not only their work, but the public’s ability to know when and how online speech is being restricted. 

The requests cite grounds including hate speech, alleged defamation of the Hindu nationalist organization Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), and concerns relating to safety and security. But the context in which these requests have emerged is particularly troubling: they target organizations and individuals whose work involves documenting restrictions on online expression and making those restrictions visible to the public. 

In other words, the organizations being targeted are among those trying to tell the public when and how its speech is being censored.

title: Civil Society Call for Scrutiny of United States’ Rights Record
content:
The United States is scheduled to appear in Geneva on November 10 for its Universal Periodic Review, the United Nations’ peer review process of every member state’s rights record. But the US is unlikely to show: the Trump administration declared in 2025 that the US would not participate.  

After the US failed to turn up in November 2025, the review was rescheduled. Should the US again fail to appear next week, it should not be given another extension and should not be exempt from this process which, as the name suggests, applies to every UN member country. 

As part of the process, US and international rights groups, including Human Rights Watch, made 192 submissions highlighting a range of human rights issues. The civil society submissions paint a worrying picture, with a dramatic worsening of the US government’s rights record over the past year.

title: JD Vance singled out Iran War for midterm rout – he didn’t say what should happen next in conflict
content:
While votes were still being counted in the U.S. midterm elections, administration figures in Washington were already inviting speculation over how the results might be connected to the conflict with Iran.

On the morning after the election, Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the major reason for the dramatic loss for Republicans was the American public’s opposition to the war. “Everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there,” he wrote, in reference to the ongoing conflict that began with U.S.-Israeli airstrikes against Iran in late February 2026.

While it is rare for a vice president to make such a critical proclamation about their own administration’s policy, President Donald Trump later stated that he did not disagree with Vance’s appraisal of the role that frustration with the Iran war played in voters’ minds.

But whether this changes Trump’s view on next steps in the ongoing conflict remains unclear. Reporting over the past few weeks has indicated that the U.S. military has been actively preparing options and increasing capabilities in the Persian Gulf region in the event the president directs a resumption of hostilities.

title: How Online Maps Lay Bare the US Military Bases Targeted by Iran
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. Become a member and support our work here.

In September, CBS News obtained new images of the aftermath of attacks on US bases in the Middle East from active service members. One told the news channel: “This is major damage to our bases that hasn’t been communicated to the American public. “We’re standing there with our eyes closed getting punched in the face,” they added.

While reports have detailed how Iran used Russian intelligence, including satellite imagery, to identify US troops, ships and aircraft, Bellingcat found that publicly available mapping platforms also reveal detailed and potentially sensitive information about US military bases in the Middle East. 

Google Maps and other online mapping services contain dozens of labels identifying facilities including headquarters, accommodation, gyms and fuel points. Publicly available photographs and videos, including material published by the US military, provide further details about how these facilities are used.

title: Turvallisuustutkimuksen hajaannuksesta koordinoituun yhteistyöhön
content:
Turun yliopisto on käynnistänyt Suomen turvallisuustutkimuskeskuksen perustamisen valmistelun yhdessä Turun korkeakouluverkoston, muiden korkeakoulujen ja viranomaisten kanssa. Keskus kokoaa eri alojen asiantuntijat kehittämään ratkaisuja puolustuksesta ja rikostorjunnasta arjen turvallisuuteen, kriisivalmiuteen ja yhteisöjen varautumiseen.

Turvallisuustutkimuskeskuksella on valtava tilaus, sillä Euroopan ja maailman turvallisuusympäristö muuttuu nopeasti. Turvallisuus on EU:ssa tutkimus-, innovaatio-, teollisuus- ja kilpailukykypolitiikan läpileikkaava teema. Suomella ja kokonaisturvallisuuden mallilla on tässä vahva asema, mutta kotimainen turvallisuustutkimus on hajanaista ja tarvitsee koordinoivan rakenteen.

title: Supermarket Attacks: Europe Can’t Wait for Russian Fingerprints
content:
A Belgian butcher is awakened at 3:30 in the morning by an employee reporting a problem with his refrigeration system. When he reaches his shop, temperatures have climbed to 18° Celsius. He estimates that about $17,000 worth of meat has been ruined. Elsewhere in Europe, supermarket workers have discovered similar problems.

The refrigeration attacks were reported in early November, around the same time that European airlines faced a wave of anonymous bomb threats. On the worst day so far, November 5, at least 21 flights had been targeted, prompting diversions, security inspections, and disruption to airline schedules. There is no established connection between the two sets of incidents.​​​ 

​​Supermarket chill cabinets and short-haul airline flights are not what most Europeans picture when they hear about Russia’s shadow war. They think of espionage, cyberattacks against government networks, suspicious fires at defense factories, or damaged infrastructure in the Baltic Sea. These are serious threats, but for most people they remain distant. A disrupted neighborhood grocery store or a grounded holiday flight is different. It brings the consequences home.

title: Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026: for a Competitive Europe
content:
Policymakers, researchers and commoners will meet in Brussels on 12 November to shape the next phase of Europe’s Digital Commons

The NGI Commons project has announced the full programme and speaker line-up for the Digital Commons Policy Summit 2026: Digital Commons and the Open Internet Stack for a Competitive Europe. The Summit will take place on Thursday 12 November 2026 at TownHall Europe in Brussels and will also be streamed online.

The Summit brings together policymakers, researchers, industry, civil society and the communities who build and maintain the Digital Commons. Together they will discuss how Europe can make open, community-governed digital infrastructure a pillar of its tech sovereignty agenda and of upcoming initiatives for sustainable European digital infrastructures.

A final event, and a look ahead

The Summit is also the final event of NGI Commons, a Coordination and Support Action that started in January 2024 and runs until February 2027. Over three years, the project’s four partners have worked to strengthen the Digital Commons and European digital infrastructures. At the Summit, they will set out their ambitions for what comes next.

title: Commons Stories: Part 3
content:
The commons is a way of structuring relationships to our resources. Instead of a property mindset, where the only question is: does someone own it? The questions in a commons are: how do we ensure this resource can be shared by all of us? What is our mutual commitment? 

Too often, I think the commons has become shorthand for “no one owns it, so no rules apply.” That is not a commons, it is a free-for-all. And in a way, it is the mirror image of the property focus of copyright maximalism because it begins and ends with whether or not the resources are or can be private property. 

It is utterly idealistic to believe that we can have spaces with shared rules, where everyone who partakes commits to the common good. Right now, on the public web, it feels like an aspiration more than a reality. It is an open question whether the internet will evolve to support and sustain public spaces that truly operate like a commons, where everyone who contributes has some say, and everyone who benefits plays by the rules. 

It is an aspiration worth fighting for. 

Next, we’ll explore the commons as resistance and the relationships that help it thrive in the final two installments of Commons Stories.

title: Gay sheep don't come cheap
content: “That one flehmened. He wants sex,” farmer Michael Stücke says, pointing to a ram (a male sheep) tilting its head up and curling its upper lip back. This way of smelling the air is known as the flehmen response, which male animals often do before mating. We’re standing in a pasture on Stücke’s sheep farm in the German town of Löhne in North Rhine-Westphalia, observing what looks like a regular flock of sheep. In reality, it may be the world’s most famous: 36 sheep, but they’re all rams, and they’re all gay. Rams that show no interest in mating with ewes (female sheep) and instead pursue other rams are relatively useless to breeders, Stücke says, so they’re usually sent to slaughter. That is, until 2023, when advertising agency Serviceplan started buying them up at auctions and giving them a permanent home on Stücke’s farm, himself a gay farmer. A friend of his working at the agency was sad to hear about what happens to gay rams, and knew he was active in an association for gay farmers. title: Missouri Voters Just Made It Much Harder for Lawmakers to Overturn Citizen-Led Initiatives
content:
Across the country on Tuesday, voters delivered a wave of Democratic victories, flipping seats in Congress as well as state legislatures, and weakening a number of Republican majorities.

Missouri was no exception. Democrats made significant gains in the state House, picking up 16 seats, though Republicans still hold every statewide office and maintain control of the legislature. 

Nonetheless, the election was more than just a rebuke of President Donald Trump. It reflected a long-simmering frustration with Missouri politicians who, time and again, have sought to override the will of voters — a practice that has intensified under years of Republican control. What’s more, voters went beyond weakening the Republican majority. They approved a constitutional amendment that curtailed the powers of the legislature and shifted more authority directly to the people.

Amendment 6, approved by a decisive margin, sharply limits the legislature’s ability to overturn laws and constitutional amendments enacted through citizen initiatives, and its ability to revive laws voters rejected through referendums.

Sedan 1947 har Finlands bokkonstkommitté valt ut samlingen Årets vackraste böcker, som visas på vandringsutställningar i Finland och runt om i Europa Till årets vackraste bok 2025 utsågs Erkka Filanders monumentala diktsamling Siemenholvi, som imponerade på juryn med sin formmässigt gränsöverskridande gestaltning.

title: Government lawyers’ lies and stonewalling endanger press freedom
content:
Government lawyers during President Donald Trump’s second term have outright lied to federal judges and refused to comply with court orders in numerous cases involving journalists and the First Amendment.

That’s according to a newly updated report from nonpartisan law and policy journal Just Security. Since last year, the journal has been evaluating the state of the “presumption of regularity” — a legal doctrine under which judges assume that the executive branch of the U.S. government is following appropriate procedures and being honest about the reasons for its actions.

That presumption was probably never warranted — after all, many of the dishonest lawyers serving in the Trump administration aren’t newcomers to the federal government. Some have been around for decades. But Just Security’s report reveals that the presumption has been consistently and shockingly undermined since Trump returned to office — leading one judge to announce that the presumption had been “destroyed.”

Judges in press freedom cases should be presuming that any claims from the administration must be heavily scrutinized.

title: Hong Kong: Human Rights Organizations Condemn Unjust Sentencing of Joshua Wong
content:
We, the undersigned organizations, condemn the November 5th sentencing of Hong Kong prodemocracy advocate Joshua Wong to a 10-year sentence by the Hong Kong High Court. This is the second time he has been sentenced under the Beijing-imposed National Security Law (NSL), which has contributed to the rapid deterioration of basic freedoms in Hong Kong.

Joshua, who marked his 30th birthday in prison three weeks ago, rose to prominence as a teenager as the cofounder of the student group Scholarism, which opposed the introduction of pro-Beijing propaganda into Hong Kong's schools. He helped lead the historic 2014 Umbrella Movement and in 2016 created the prodemocracy Demosistō party, which was forced to disband after the approval of the NSL in 2020. He has received international acclaim for his democratic activism, including multiple nominations for the Nobel Peace Prize.

title: What comes after networked authoritarianism?
content:
October’s Spotlight contributors illuminated a range of political, economic, and geographic contexts

Originally published on Global Voices

Image by Gerd Altmann on Pixabay.

Fifteen years ago I wrote an article about “networked authoritarianism,” describing China as “exhibit A” for how an authoritarian state adapts to the internet and then adapts digital technologies to increase its own power. I sought to counter prevailing narratives of the time that the internet and tech companies were intrinsically a liberating, democratizing force. While such narratives were eventually discredited, we must not give up on our ability to use technology to defend and exercise our rights. Nor can we simply demand that governments and companies solve the problems they jointly continue to create.

October’s spotlight on Big Tech and Authoritarianism explored a range of relationships between tech companies and political actors across the global majority. Power is wielded through digital technologies in many ways. There are no quick fixes or easy solutions to stop abuses.

title: OPINION: Iran: Compromise or Catastrophe
content:
By Alon Ben-Meir*

NEW YORK | 5 November 2026 (IDN) — There is no durable military solution to the American-Israeli conflict with Iran. Bombs can destroy installations, but they cannot erase scientific knowledge, extinguish national pride, or create a sustainable political settlement.

The choice is not between demonstrating strength and accepting weakness; it is between negotiating enforceable compromises and courting a catastrophe that could engulf the Middle East. Trump must recognize that understanding Iran’s history, security calculations, and determination to preserve its sovereignty is the indispensable starting point for diplomacy.

Trump’s fundamental failure has been to confuse overwhelming military power with an understanding of the adversary. Before negotiating with—or attacking—another country, a president must examine its history, national identity, geography, strategic military capabilities, resilience, and perception of existential threats. Understanding these factors does not excuse the Iranian regime’s repression or regional aggression. It makes American diplomacy and negotiation strategies more effective.

title: Save Our Stories: Why Libraries Need the Law on Their Side
content:
Today, 5 November, is World Digital Preservation Day, and this year’s theme, “Save our Stories (SOS): Our digital heritage in danger”, could not be more timely for libraries.

Few missions are more central to libraries than preservation. From local history collections in public libraries to rare books in academic centres and the full national bibliographies held by national libraries, ensuring that the past and present survive into the future is a core role.

Preservation, crucially, is less about an attachment to the past than about an investment in the future. Without it, researchers, communities, and citizens are all the poorer. Access to facts, records and ideas is vital for study, democratic transparency, and the fulfilment of cultural rights.

There are therefore plenty of reasons to be concerned about a 21st-century black hole in library collections that is only getting deeper.

title: Hunajaa valtion vihollisen kanssa
content:
Ajoimme nelivetoisella jeepillä läpi Tigrayn vuoristoa. Vuosi oli 2021, ja sota pohjoisessa Etiopiassa oli raivonnut jo yli puoli vuotta. Pysähdyimme pieneen kylään, ja ympärillä alkoi vilkas keskustelu ja kova kuhina. Olin sanonut, että olisi kiinnostavaa päästä haastattelemaan paikallisten kapinallisten sotilaita heidän ajatuksistaan.
Se kyllä järjestyisi, ja järjestyipä toinenkin haastattelu.

Yhtäkkiä istuin savitalossa jakkaralla pienen pöydän äärellä. Pöydällä oli purkki tuoretta hunajaa ja jokaiselle lusikka. Vastapäätä istui ­Getachew Reda, Etiopian entinen viestintäministeri ja silloinen kapinallisjohtaja. Hän oli hallituksen halutuimpia henkilöitä, elävänä tai kuolleena. Mieluiten kuolleena.

Emme me häntä tietenkään sattumalta löytäneet, vaan hän halusi tulla löydetyksi ja kertoa asiansa. Myös muutama muu kollega oli pääsyt hänen juttusilleen, mutta esimerkiksi ruotsalainen kilpailijani sairastui koronaan eikä päässyt lähtemään maasta. Voitin uutiskilpailun.

title: Culture is back on the Horizon – Parliament compromise text
content:
The Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund, welcomes the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

The compromise text was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme, signalling an important shift in how the role of arts and culture in research and innovation is understood.

title: Using personalisation makes every AI chat less risky and more effective — here are five essential custom instructions to add
content:
One of best things you can do to lower the risks of using AI and improve the quality of outputs is to spend five minutes with one of AI tools’ least-used features: their personalisation settings.

ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot and Claude all have personalisation features: a section of the tool where you can give it permanent extra information that informs every conversation. You can find it in your general settings under names like ‘instructions’, ‘personal context’ or ‘personalization’, or using the links above.

Here are five instructions you can include in that section:

Your professional role, ethics, location, language, skill level and other details all provide vital context that will help reduce assumptions and misunderstandings and improve the ‘predictions’ that AI tools make when responding.

title: What the US midterms result means for the Ukraine war
content:
The US midterm elections have shifted the balance of power in Congress, delivering a massive blow to Donald Trump and his Republican party. This has implications both at home and possibly abroad, including for US policy towards Ukraine; an issue that was hardly mentioned during the campaigns.

But even if Ukraine did not figure much in the election, the question in US politics of what to do about the war has not gone away. Indeed, in the weeks and months before the result was announced, Trump had been busily rowing back on US support for Ukraine. This was despite much opposition, even from some Republicans.

Crucial intelligence to Kyiv about Russian strikes was cut off, before later being reinstated, while critical military aid was reduced. Trump also decided to suspend several sanctions on Russia.

This move was denounced by President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine as only helping Russia, but justified by Trump as being “in the national interests of the United States” and also a decision that might help his party’s electoral chances by reducing gas prices.

title: Why AI cannot ‘think’ like humans do
content:
Today’s artificial intelligence technologies have become remarkably good at generating text and ideas that seem profoundly human. Chatbots powered by large language models such as ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini and Perplexity AI can write poems, brainstorm and find solutions to complex problems.

The developers of these products drew heavily on the human brain for inspiration, creating artificial neural networks based on the workings of human neurons. Their systems now produce outputs that often resemble the outputs of human thinking.

AI and the human mind, however, do not work the same way. Similar results do not necessarily mean similar processes.

“World models” are an emerging technology that could help AI systems move closer to human “thinking” by helping them learn to anticipate what might happen and use that prediction to act. Still, AI will not perceive, learn or understand the world as humanity does.

title: WiNoDa Conference 2026 “Beyond drawers and spreadsheets: the journey of object-related data” – a lively community event
content:
With participants in the conference room of the Museum für Naturkunde Berlin and numerous people joining online, at 9:30 in the morning of October 21, 2026, we declared the conference “Beyond drawers and spreadsheets: the journey of object-related data” officially open.

We kicked off the conference with an introduction from our coordinator, Cora Albrecht, who warmly welcomed participants and then briefly introduced WiNoDa and some of its milestones from the last two years.

Then Mareike Petersen, head of the Science Programme “Collection Future” at MfN, nicely framed the day’s topic, highlighting how much data can be extracted from collections of natural objects while also noting some of the most common challenges in working with historical information. WiNoDa’s learning offers aim to lower the access barrier to this data, making it useful for researchers and museum staff around the world.

After the introductory talk, it was time for our community. We received numerous excellent submissions for the conference from the following subject areas:

  • Collection management and standardisation
  • Data reuse for research and conservation
  • Digitisation workflows
  • AI and computational methods

title: Everyone Everywhere Hated Meta’s New AI Training Terms. Now, They’re On Pause
content:
Following widespread backlash, Meta announced earlier this week it’s putting a planned update of its commercial terms of use on pause. The terms would have required business accounts to allow Meta to “use any content from such domains, web pages, or URLs to provide, develop, improve, research, train, and maintain the integrity of” Meta’s products. 

The new terms were initially set to go into effect on October 30, but after outcry from journalists and users who didn’t want Meta reaching far beyond Instagram and Facebook and into their websites to suck up their work as training data for its generative AI products, Meta announced it was pushing the change to November 20. Now, it’s on hold entirely. 

“We recently shared that we were updating the Meta Commercial Terms, Product Catalog Terms, Self-Serve Ad Terms, and Ad Creative Generative AI Terms,” Meta says on the page where the commercial terms announcement used to be. “These updates are now paused and will not take effect on November 20, 2026. We are continuing to consult with stakeholders and will provide a further update when we have more to share. In the meantime, our existing terms remain in effect.”

title: Israel/OPT: Israel must immediately release Palestinian farmer and land defender Ghassan Najjar
content:
In response to the Israeli military’s arrest of Palestinian farmer and land defender Ghassan Najjar during a pre-dawn raid on the village of Burin south of Nablus in the northern occupied West Bank, on 27 October, Erika Guevara Rosas, Amnesty International’s Senior Director for Research, Policy, Advocacy and Campaigns, said:

“Israeli authorities must immediately release Ghassan Najjar who was arrested solely because of his peaceful activism to protect the olive harvest season in Burin. Israeli intelligence agents had explicitly threatened Ghassan Najjar, co-founder of Burin’s Land and Farming Agricultural Cooperative, that he would be arrested if he did not stop his activism. His activism includes community organizing, supporting mutual aid among farmers through the cooperative, organizing an annual Kite Festival in the village and leading numerous cultural initiatives. Ghassan Najjar had been facing repeated threats since the start of the olive harvest season and their frequency intensified during the week prior to his arrest.

title: Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit
content:
The centrepiece of every UN climate summit is for countries to negotiate the wording of a large number of legal agreements – and COP31 in the Turkish city of Antalya is no different.

These texts are hashed out behind closed doors in the “blue zone” at the COP, where diplomats from nearly 200 nations – not including the US – will be haggling over each individual verb.

Over the course of the two-week summit, negotiators will be trying to reach consensus on more than 100 separate agreements – but, first, they must agree which issues are on the agenda.

The complexity of this process can make it challenging to keep track of what countries are fighting about and how negotiations are progressing.

Carbon Brief’s real-time text tracker, below, offers a helping hand by decoding the agenda and keeping a searchable record of every document for each part of the negotiations.

The first column of the interactive tracker lists the topic of each agenda item, with further columns including dates, page counts and links to the original PDFs.

The table is searchable via the interactive text box and can be sorted using the arrow icons.

title: "They Have Eyes": How Trump's Corruption Became a Top Concern for Midterm Voters
content:
Democrats regained control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s historic midterm elections, a comeback fueled largely by voter anger over high prices and the war on Iran. But surveys also found that corruption was a major concern, with 76% of voters telling a Harris poll that elected officials care more about enriching themselves than improving the economy for ordinary people. A separate Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 63% of Americans considered it inappropriate for Trump and his family to profit from cryptocurrency, while 69% said his private business interests influence his decisions as president.

“If this election was about corruption and cost, then this next Congress needs to be focused on accountability and affordability,” says Donald Sherman, the president and CEO of Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington, or CREW.

title: Reflecting on Digital Rights Wins and Losses in Sacramento
content:
California’s 2026 legislative session has officially adjourned and it’s time to reflect on the wins and losses that have shaped Californians’ digital rights landscape this year. This was the second year of a two-year legislative session, which meant several bills resumed their legislative paths from 2025.

EFF monitored nearly 100 bills in the state over the two-year session. These included proposed regulations on 3D printers, access to social media platforms, police, commercial, and workplace surveillance practices, AI, and other privacy concerns. While we saw some victories, alarming developments also raised serious concerns about the future of privacy protection in the state.

Governor Newsom signed vital protections on the use of automated decision-making in the workplace and workplace surveillance tools, specifically No Robo Bosses (SB 947) and AB 1883.

Kävijät pääsevät tutustumaan muun muassa robotiikkaan, konenäköön ja tekoälyn hyödyntämiseen sekä 3D-tulostukseen ja hyvinvointia tukeviin teknologioihin. Tutkimuskeskuksen asiantuntijat esittelevät laitteita ja ratkaisuja, kertovat niiden käyttötavoista ja vastaavat kävijöiden kysymyksiin. Osaa teknologioista pääsee myös kokeilemaan itse.

Tapahtuma sopii kaikenikäisille, eikä osallistuminen edellytä teknologian tuntemusta. Mukaan voi tulla vaikka koko perheen kanssa.

RoboAI-yhteiskäyttölaboratoriossa voi tutustua erityisesti robotiikkaan ja teollisuuden teknologioihin. Yksi illan kiinnostavista tuttavuuksista on ihmisen kaltainen Aatos-humanoidirobotti. Esillä oleva tutkimus auttaa ymmärtämään, miten robotiikkaa, konenäköä ja tekoälyä voidaan hyödyntää esimerkiksi yritysten toiminnassa ja työn kehittämisessä.

RoboAI Cyberlabissa tutustutaan kyberturvallisuuteen ja opiskelijoiden rakentamaan supertietokoneeseen. Tieteen tietotekniikan keskus CSC:n lahjoittamista osista rakennettu kokonaisuus palvelee SAMKissa opetusta ja tutkimusta. Lisäksi kuullaan myös avaruusteknologiaan liittyvästä toiminnasta.

title: UNICEF: Vesijärjestelmiä tuhoavat iskut ovat kolminkertaistuneet, lapset konfliktien keskellä eivät saa puhdasta vettä
content:
Vesi- ja sanitaatiojärjestelmiä tuhonneiden iskujen määrä konflikteissa on kolminkertaistunut vuosien 2021 ja 2025 välillä. Tämä lisää lasten riskiä altistua tautiepidemioille, aliravitsemukselle ja väkivallalle, kertoo UNICEFin uusi raportti Water Under Fire Volume 4.

– Hyökkäykset riistävät lapsilta turvallisen juomaveden. Humanitaariset työntekijät tekevät parhaansa taatakseen vedensaannin. Korjaukset eivät kuitenkaan voi korvata sitä, että vesijärjestelmiä on suojeltava kansainvälisen humanitaarisen oikeuden mukaisesti, sanoo UNICEFin pääjohtaja Catherine Russell.

Raportissa kuvataan seitsemän eri tapaa, joilla vesi- ja sanitaatiojärjestelmiä vastaan hyökätään. Ne vaihtelevat iskuista puhdistuslaitoksiin ja vesilähteisiin aina vedenpuhdistukseen tarvittavien varaosien ja kemikaalien saatavuuden rajoittamiseen.

Burkina Fasossa yli 145 vesipistettä tuhottiin hyökkäyksissä vuosina 2020–2025 katkaisten vedensaannin 830 000 ihmiseltä, joista yli puolet oli lapsia. Lokakuun 2023 jälkeen Gazassa yli 130 00 metriä jätevesiputkia on vaurioitunut ja käsittelemätöntä jätevettä on johdettu Välimereen tai väliaikaisille säilytysalueille.

title: RCH Partnership launches its first Joint Transnational Call
content:
The European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage (RCH) has opened its first Joint Transnational Call, with a total budget of €36 million. The call will support international research on how climate and environmental change affect cultural heritage, and on how heritage can help societies become more resilient.

Titled “Foundations for climate-resilient cultural heritage: Assessing and managing impact and risk, dealing with damage and loss”, the call opened on 4 November 2026. Pre-proposals are due by 11 January 2027 at 14:00 CET.

This is the first call launched by RCH, a ten-year European Partnership (2026–2035) co-funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe, which brings together 90 partners from 30 countries. With climate change already putting heritage at risk, the call encourages projects that combine scientific research, innovation and community knowledge to develop practical tools and policies.

Proposals must address at least one of four interconnected sub-themes, and may combine several:

  • Risk and impact assessment, and cultural heritage risk preparedness and management
  • Managing loss and damage of cultural heritage impacted by climate change-induced natural hazards

title: In Rio, A Celebration of Life
content:
It takes a long time to read more than a hundred names. I stood holding a white balloon alongside the victims’ relatives, some wearing T-shirts bearing photos of their loved ones. The list went on and on. As Tauã Brito said name after name, as if reading tombstones, the scale of the tragedy hit me. Then she reached Wellington Brito Santos, her 20-year-old son. He, like the others, had been killed during a police operation on October 28, 2025.

One year later, we stood at the very spot where residents had laid out dozens of bodies that police had abandoned in a forested area of Complexo da Penha, a cluster of favelas in Rio de Janeiro.

When she finished reading the names, we released our balloons. They rose past the tangle of utility wires overhead, above the narrow alleys of the favelas, toward the sky over Rio. Passionate locals call it the Cidade Maravilhosa, the Marvelous City.

A colleague asked me how I was doing. I started to cry.

title: Building The New Equilibrium Economy
content:
More than 2,000 years ago, Aristotle formulated one of history’s most remarkable thought experiments. What, he asked, would happen if tools could obey commands, even anticipate them? What would happen if they could carry out their work entirely on their own?

“If every instrument could accomplish its own work, obeying or anticipating the will of others,” he wrote in “Politics” around 350 B.C.E., “if the shuttle would weave and the plectrum touch the lyre without a hand to guide them, chief workmen would not need servants, nor masters slaves.”

For centuries, this passage was understood primarily as a philosophical allegory. Today, what is striking is not Aristotle’s technical imagination but his political imagination. He was more interested in the social consequences of self-operating machines than in their feasibility.

Artificial intelligence forces us to confront this issue anew: What becomes of a society whose economy, purpose and welfare state are built on wage labor if wage labor loses that foundational role? Perhaps the true AI revolution will begin in our conception of what it means to be human, not inside Silicon Valley’s data centers.

title: Cyber Incident Disrupts French Blood Storage Systems
content:
The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said a cybersecurity incident involving one of its refrigeration equipment providers disrupted cold storage systems at three of its sites, causing temperature and defrost settings to rise to unusually high levels.

The incident occurred on November 2, according to a statement published by EFS the following day. The organization said it was not directly targeted, but the attack on its provider affected systems used to monitor and control refrigeration units.

EFS said its alarm systems enabled staff to respond promptly, ensuring that no blood samples or products were compromised. As a precaution, the contents of the affected refrigeration units were transferred to other facilities.

The statement confirmed information reported earlier by the French satirical newspaper Le Canard enchaîné, which identified refrigeration equipment provider Coolworld as the apparent target of the incident.

Coolworld also acknowledged a cybersecurity incident involving remote monitoring software used in refrigeration systems, although it did not explicitly link the incident to EFS.

title: The Man Who Risked His Life Mocking the Nazis: Read 96 Issues of His Underground Magazine, Created in Hiding During WWII
content:
The word zine, referring to a homemade magazine not distributed through the normal commercial channels, has a longer history than you might expect. Its earliest recorded uses date from 1946 in the world of pulp magazines, most often of the science-fiction variety. But just a year earlier, as it happens, one of the most historically notable zines avant la lettre concluded publication. The end of World War II had everything to do with it, since Het Onderwater-Cabaret, or The Underwater Cabaret, existed as a rebuke against the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Over its two-year run, it put out 96 issues, totaling over 1,700 pages full of art and poems — all created by one man in hiding in an attic.

Born to a Jewish family in Dortmund in 1908, Curt Bloch studied law with aspirations of becoming a judge. When Hitler rose to power, his plans changed: he first left for Amsterdam, and later, when Germany invaded the Netherlands in 1940, he had to keep moving until he ended up in the border town of Enschede.

title: France, US clash over G7 effort on AI safety
content:
The U.S. government has scuttled a French push for the G7 to coordinate on advanced AI safety, with a White House official calling it “unnecessary bureaucracy.”

France’s digital minister Anne Le Hénanff told a French Senate hearing on Wednesday that she held two ministerial meetings in September and October to secure G7 commitments to a high-level working group to test frontier AI — the most advanced models — and share information about risks and incidents.

That effort “did not reach a successful conclusion” because the U.S. wanted to pursue its own approach, the French minister said.

“They are not prepared, at this stage, to issue a joint statement with the other six G7 nations, and have asked us to wait for the findings of their own assessment,” said Le Hénanff. “Naturally, we regret this, but we are continuing to move forward as Europeans on this issue.”

A White House official, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said that the French government proposed a “poorly defined body” to cooperate on AI that the administration feared would “create unnecessary bureaucracy.”

title: SLS lanserar nya stöd för forskning, litteratur och digitalisering av kulturarv – och stärker humaniora genom ny satsning
content:

Produktionsstöd för att stödja professionella bokutgivare att bibehålla en bred utgivning av hög kvalitet och därigenom främja mångfalden av litteratur som utkommer på svenska i Finland. Stödet kan till exempel användas för redaktionell bearbetning, grafisk formgivning, tryckkostnader och produktion av e-böcker och ljudböcker.

title: Preparing the web for post-quantum cryptography
content:
The Sovereign Tech Fund commissions more than €1 million of work to make Let's Encrypt, which secures a large share of the web, ready for quantum computers.

We have committed more than €1 million to prepare the web for post-quantum cryptography, encryption that is designed to withstand quantum computers. Through the Sovereign Tech Fund, we have contracted the Internet Security Research Group (ISRG) to move Let's Encrypt to Merkle Tree Certificates, a new format for website certificates that stays secure in the quantum era.

Let's Encrypt is the free, automated service that issues website certificates for a large share of the web. A website certificate is a digital document that lets your browser confirm two things: that you reached the website you typed in, and that nobody on the network can read or change what you send.

title: Miesten kokema väkivalta jää usein piiloon
content:
Miesten kokema väkivalta voi jättää pitkäaikaisia psyykkisiä, fyysisiä, sosiaalisia ja taloudellisia seurauksia. Miessakit-järjestön pitkän aikavälin asiakastyössä ovat nousseet esiin erityisesti häpeä, yksinäisyys, epäonnistumisen kokemukset ja pelko omien lasten menettämisestä.

Järjestön mukaan miesten väkivaltakokemuksia ei aina tunnisteta tai oteta vakavasti, mikä voi entisestään vaikeuttaa avun hakemista.

"Kymmenen vuoden asiakastyön perusteella tiedämme, että moni mies kokee tulevansa vähätellyksi tai ettei häneltä edes kysytä väkivallan kokemuksista ja niiden seurauksista. Uhrin kokemuksen vakavuutta ei pitäisi arvioida sukupuolen perusteella", sanoo Miessakit ry:n väkivaltatyöntekijä Jussi Pekkola järjestön tiedotteessa.

Pekkolan mukaan kokemusten sivuuttaminen voi syventää häpeää ja vahvistaa tunnetta epäonnistumisesta miehenä. Moni vetäytyy yksinäisyyteen. Vakavimmillaan vähättely ja kohtaamattomuus voivat johtaa itsetuhoisiin ajatuksiin tai tekoihin.

Tilastokeskuksen vuonna 2023 julkaiseman väestötutkimuksen mukaan 18 prosenttia 18–74-vuotiaista miehistä oli kokenut elämänsä aikana fyysistä väkivaltaa parisuhdekumppaninsa taholta. Naisilla vastaava osuus oli 34 prosenttia.

title: HER – Å forelske seg i KI
content:
Filmvisning og samtale på Vega Scene, onsdag 2. desember kl. 17.30

Samtale med filmskaper Tonje Hessen Schei, psykolog og forfatter Sissel Gran og professor Petter Bae Brandtzæg, ledet av Tellef Raabe, prosjektleder i Fritt Ord.

Theodore lever av å skrive inderlige brev på vegne av folk som ikke klarer det selv. Så forelsker han seg i operativsystemet sitt. Da regissør Spike Jonzes moderne klassiker Her kom i 2013, var denne ideen science fiction. I dag har millioner av mennesker daglige samtaler med KI-assistenter som husker hva de har fortalt, svarer med varm stemme og alltid har tid.

Her, med Joaquin Phoenix i hovedrollen og Scarlett Johansson som stemmen til Samantha, vant Oscar og Golden Globe for beste originalmanus. Filmen står igjen som kanskje den mest presise skildringen av hva som skjer når teknologien flytter inn i det mest private. Og virkeligheten imiterer fiksjonen: Da OpenAI lanserte sin taleassistent i 2024, la toppsjef Sam Altman ut ett ord på X: «her». Stemmen hørtes ut som Johanssons.

title: Hallitus esittää lakiuudistusta kehittyvien maiden investointihankkeita tukevaan rahoitusmalliin
content:
Hallitus esittää uutta lakia kehittyviin maihin myönnettävistä tuetuista investointiluotoista. Tavoitteena on parantaa suomalaisten yritysten edellytyksiä osallistua kehittyvien maiden julkisiin investointihankkeisiin sekä vahvistaa tuen valvontaa ja oikeusvarmuutta. Esitys tukee myös Suomen osallistumista Ukrainan jälleenrakentamiseen. Ulkoministeriössä valmistellulla uudistuksella ajanmukaistetaan vuonna 2000 säädettyä lainsäädäntöä, selkeytetään rahoitusmallin sääntöjä ja laajennetaan mahdollisuuksia järjestää hankkeiden rahoitusta.

Tuetuissa investointiluotoissa yhdistyvät ulkopuolisen luotonantajanmyöntämä laina ja kehitysyhteistyövaroista rahoitettava tuki. Rahoitusmallilla alennetaan kehittyvien maiden investointikustannuksia, edistetään kestävää kehitystä ja hyödynnetään suomalaista osaamista ja teknologiaa.

”Esitys parantaa suomalaisten yritysten toimintamahdollisuuksia kehittyvissä maissa ja vahvistaa niiden osallistumista kehitysyhteistyöhön ja kehitysrahoitukseen entisestään. Tavoite on kirjattu hallitusohjelmaan. Hankkeita on jo nyt muun muassa terveydenhuollon, energian ja meteorologian aloilla”, ulkomaankauppa- ja kehitysministeri Ville Tavio sanoo.

title: What Everyone Gets Wrong About Genocide
content:
Genocide, as set out in the UN’s 1948 convention, has a 26-word definition that has caused problems its authors probably never imagined. 

The convention sums up the crime thus: “Genocide means any of the following acts committed with intent to destroy, in whole or in part, a national, ethnical, racial or religious group as such.” It then lists those acts, including killing or otherwise harming the group. 

But that apparently simple sentence contains a chain of ambiguities. Is Ukraine a genocide? Is Gaza? Or the October 7 attacks in Israel? Reaching back to the past, is it true to describe European or Arab slavers as guilty of genocide (if the convention had existed then)? 

The answer depends partly on interpretation. This is in vivid contrast to other war law, where meanings are clear. The International Criminal Court’s statute, for instance, has no problem explaining two of its core crimes: war crimes and Crimes Against Humanity. There are no ambiguities. No disputes. Everyone can understand them. But the third core crime is different. Genocide’s definition radiates uncertainty.

title: CDIF Releases Initial Converters for Domain Standards
content:
Resources for the Cross Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF) have just been expanded to include a series of converters for metadata encoded in a range of domain standards. These converters are developed in Python, and provide transformations both to and from the relevant CDIF profiles. Each is accompanied by a set of example metadata. The conversions cover Croissant ML, Science on Schema.org (SOSO), DDI Codebook, the FAIR2 specification, DCAT, the NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) Unified Metadata Model – Collections, DDI-CDI, and RO Crate.

The mappings used in the converters are published in the Simple Standard for Sharing Ontological Mappings (SSSOM) format, for modification and reuse. The converters use a combination of SSSOM mapping and transforms implemented by the python code; the documentation for each converted explains the workflow.

title: Your family's social status still determines yours
content: France, Germany, Portugal, the Netherlands, Italy, and beyond. Young people were once again on the streets across Europe last Saturday. These protests had different triggers, for instance anger over school conditions in France, or opposition to the potential return of conscription in Germany. But there's one shared, underlying frustration: many young people feel that they won't have a better life than their parents. And there are reasons for that feeling. A decades-long development is coming to a head: social mobility has stalled across much of Europe. It refers to the ability to move up – or down – the social and economic ladder – a core promise of liberal democracy. It's mainly measured by occupation, income, and education level. Can someone whose parents never went to university get a degree? Can they find a job that pays better than their parents' work does? Increasingly, the answer to both questions is no. In an “average OECD country”, it takes around four to five generations for children from the poorest 10% of households to reach the mean income levels, according to the organisation itself. title: Trump’s State Department Is Giving $1 Million to Controversial Group to Study Crimes Against White South Africans
content:
After slashing funding for programs that documented atrocities and protected human rights abroad, President Donald Trump’s State Department is now granting one of its first new human rights awards to a controversial South African organization that promotes the disputed notion that white farmers are a violently targeted, persecuted group, according to multiple sources knowledgeable about the funding. 

The group expected to receive the nearly $1 million award, AfriForum, is a nonprofit that advocates on behalf of Afrikaners, a subset of South Africa’s white population. The organization says its members, who have a “God-given calling,” fight for Afrikaner interests and self-governance. The money will be used to “document hateful rhetoric and violent acts” against Afrikaners and other minority populations in the country.

title: Unmarried Chinese women are rewriting the marriage script
content:
Chinese women are challenging marriage pressures and redefining what it means to be single.

Originally published on Global Voices

The marriage market at People’s Park in Shanghai, 2013. Photo by Jpbowen via Wikimedia Commons, licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

On weekends at Shanghai’s People’s Park, umbrellas covered with handwritten sheets of paper line the paths. Parents stand beside them, exchanging information about their unmarried children: age, height, education, income, and whether they own an apartment. It is one of China’s most famous marriage markets — a place where private hopes and social expectations meet in public since 2005.

For years, the word shengnü (剩女), literally translated as “leftover women,” hovered over many of the women whose profiles appeared there.

The translation sounds strange in English because the original Chinese carries a sharper meaning. The character sheng (剩) does not simply mean “remaining.” It suggests something left behind, something unused. In everyday contexts, it can describe leftover food — something that has passed its ideal moment and may eventually be discarded.

Chinese women are challenging marriage pressures and redefining what it means to be single.

title: OPINION: African Countries Face Rising Economic Risks
content:
By Daniel D. Bradlow*

PRETORIA | 5 November 2026 (IDN) —The current global economic situation is confusing. On the one hand, it’s characterised by inflation and food and other critical supply shortages caused by the wars in Ukraine and the Gulf states. On the other, by optimism and economic growth caused by the boom in AI investments.

The situation both poses threats and offers opportunities to Africa.

On the upside, the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank are predicting that African growth will be around 4.5% in 2026 and 2027. This is higher than the IMF’s estimates of 3.1% global growth in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027.

The IMF maintains that African countries are reaping the rewards of the painful macro-economic reforms that they undertook earlier in the century. The reforms are helping African governments weather the shocks caused by the wars in Ukraine and the Gulf.

But the World Bank has warned that 2027 African poverty levels will be higher than they were in 2022. UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD) reports that since 2010, the continent’s public debt has increased at about four times the rate at which its GDP has grown.

title: Dementia with Lewy bodies: what you should know about the little-known, progressive brain disease
content:
Robin Williams, Monica Vitti, Patrick Stewart or French actress Nathalie Baye: all these famous people lost their lives to dementia with Lewy bodies.

This neurocognitive disease is only tends to get publicity when a celebrity dies from it. Yet it is a common disease (and one of the most common forms of dementia), in France alone it affects about 250,000 people, which makes it the country’s second most widespread neurodegenerative disease, after Alzheimer’s, putting on a par with Parkinson’s. It is estimated that dementia with Lewy bodies (commonly known as “DLB”) affects more than 10 million patients worldwide.

What causes the disease? What symptoms should we look out for? How is it treated? Here is what you need to know.

Dementia with Lewy bodies owes its name to inclusions that develop inside patients’ neurons called “Lewy bodies”, after the German-born doctor Friedrich Heinrich Lewy, who first discovered their existence in 1912.

However, it was only in 1976 that the first clinical case was formally described, while the first international clinical criteria were defined much later in 1996.

title: Delayed international support has hampered efforts to contain and treat Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo
content:
I visited a family of 19 in Sierra Leone in 2015. By the time I arrived, eight had died. The other 11 were left to live with the grief and fear of what might happen next.

I am a medical doctor and epidemiologist, and at that time I was serving on an African Union Ebola response mission. The 2014-16 epidemic in West Africa caused more than 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths. Over roughly six months in Sierra Leone, I saw how quickly the disease could overwhelm families and health services.

That’s also when I learned that good medical advice can fail if people do not trust those delivering it. Some families buried relatives secretly, despite warnings. In certain communities, funeral practices included washing the body and sprinkling water on mourners, which risked exposing people to infected bodily fluids.

Simply repeating instructions did not help. But those of us working in the field found that working with families to make burials safer while respecting their grief helped them to mourn their loss while stopping the virus from spreading.

title: Oldest Evidence of Getting High on Cannabis Discovered In 2,800-Year-Old Tomb: ‘Absolutely Crazy’
content:
Archaeologists have discovered the oldest direct evidence of psychoactive cannabis use in a Siberian tomb that dates back 2,800 years and was the site of human and horse sacrifices, according to a study published on Thursday in Science. 

During excavations of the tomb, a team found more than 1,400 cannabis seeds scattered around the remains of several Iron Age individuals, and even identified cannabinoids—including the active compound tetrahydrocannabinol (THC)—in a person’s preserved hair. 

Though humans cultivated cannabis for many millennia before the Iron Age, this is by far the earliest clear-cut proof that the plant was consumed for its psychoactive effects, which have made it one of the most widely used drugs in the world today.

The discovery is “absolutely crazy,” said Gino Caspari, an archaeologist at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology and the University of Bern who led the study, in a call with 404 Media. “People have been speculating a lot about psychoactive use of cannabis in the past, but to actually pin it down and prove it with soft tissue evidence of the humans involved—that is something very special.
