title: Hong Kong: Cruel Joshua Wong sentence a grim reminder of city’s disdain for human rights
content:
Responding to the 10-year sentence handed to Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong for “colluding with foreign forces”, Amnesty International’s Deputy Regional Director Sarah Brooks said:

“The Hong Kong authorities’ persecution of Joshua Wong continues with this latest national security conviction, which cruelly – and perhaps deliberately – comes mere months before he would have been eligible for release under his previous conviction.

“Joshua Wong’s bravery in speaking truth to power should be commended, but instead in Hong Kong it makes him a criminal. Today’s sentence is another grim reminder of how Hong Kong’s National Security Law has become a tool to punish dissent rather than to genuinely protect national security.

“The international community should not accept the continued criminalization of legitimate activism as the new normal in Hong Kong. Governments must continue to press for the protection of human rights and the release of those imprisoned solely for exercising their rights.

title: First Gen Z Congresswoman: DSA's Melat Kiros on Corruption, Medicare for All & Israel
content:
The Democratic Socialists of America made major gains in this year’s U.S. midterms, electing not just the largest-ever socialist bloc to Congress, but also winning dozens of races at the state, county and municipal levels. Democracy Now! spoke with Congressmember-elect Melat Kiros on election night following her victory in Denver, Colorado. She identified Medicare for All as her top priority and said progressives must lay the groundwork “so that in ’29, when we have the House, the Senate and the White House, we can sign it into law on day one.”

Kiros is a 29-year-old Ethiopian immigrant and lawyer. In 2023, Kiros wrote an open letter about the danger of conflating antisemitism and criticism of Israel, for which she was fired by her law firm. She won a major upset in the Democratic primary earlier this year against longtime incumbent Congressmember Diana DeGette.

title: Join EFF to Celebrate the Life of Aaron Swartz
content:
Join us to celebrate the legacy of Aaron Swartz on Nov. 8, 2026. With the organizers of Aaron Swartz Day, we’re honoring his life with an in-person and remote hackathon. This event is supported by several organizations that carry on his work, including the Internet Archive—which is hosting the in-person event—the Freedom of the Press Foundation, Creative Commons and the Free Law Project.

Aaron Swartz was a digital rights champion who believed in the need for an open internet. His life was cut short in 2013, after federal prosecutors charged him under the Computer Fraud and Abuse Act (CFAA) for systematically downloading academic journal articles from the online database JSTOR. Facing the prospect of a long and unjust sentence, Aaron died by suicide at the age of 26.

EFF was proud to call Aaron a friend and ally. We continue to stand with programmers and developers engaged in cutting-edge exploration of technology through our Coders' Rights Project.

title: Työviikon lyhentäminen ei suojaa tekoälyn vaikutuksilta
content:
Tekoälyn tuottavuushyötyjä kannattaa tavoitella uudistamalla työtä ja vahvistamalla osaamista. Työajan lyhentäminen lähinnä kiihdyttäisi työpaikkojen tuhoa, kirjoittaa Etla-kolumnissaan Antti Kauhanen.

Helsingin Sanomissa julkaistussa kirjoituksessa ”Pelko tekoälyn aiheuttamasta massa­työttömyydestä ajaa maailmalla etsimään ratkaisuja” esitettiin työviikon lyhentämistä ratkaisuksi tekoälyn työmarkkinavaikutuksiin.

Ajatus perustuu oletukseen, että työtä on tulevaisuudessa vähemmän ja jäljelle jäävä työ kannattaa jakaa useammalle.

Tutkimusnäyttö ei tue tätä päättelyä.

Tekoälyn vaikutukset työllisyyteen ovat toistaiseksi olleet vähäisiä, eikä teknologian nopeakaan kehitys tarkoita äkillistä työmarkkinamurrosta.

Tekoälyn hyödyntäminen edellyttää työtapojen ja organisaatioiden uudistamista, mikä vie aikaa. Tekoäly korvaa tehtäviä, mutta myös täydentää ihmistyötä, parantaa tuottavuutta ja synnyttää uusia tehtäviä. Automatisoituvien tehtävien määrä ei siten kerro työllisyyden kokonaismuutoksesta.

Työajan lyhentäminen ei puolestaan luo työpaikkoja vain siksi, että kukin tekee vähemmän töitä. Työn määrä ei ole vakio. Työpaikkojen syntyminen ja säilyminen riippuvat työllistämisen kannattavuudesta.

title: Bangladesh Labor Protests Turn Violent
content:
Bangladesh police have used batons and tear gas to disperse thousands of garment workers protesting for higher wages. Violence by thugs allegedly linked to factory owners and political parties, arson, factory vandalism, and attacks on police have all been reported. 

Consistent with international standards, Bangladesh authorities should ensure that police use force only when necessary and proportionate, and that those responsible for violence are held accountable.

A garment worker, Toufiq Hossain, died on November 3. A co-worker who had been with him told Human Rights Watch: “We were returning to the factory [after lunch] when Toufiq got caught between protesting workers and men hired to tackle the protest by another garment factory. When I looked back, I saw Toufiq lying on the ground. The hired men had beaten him brutally.”

The striking workers are seeking a monthly wage of 30,000 taka (US$241), up from the 12,500 taka set in 2023. The government formed a wage board on November 1, which announced that a new pay structure, once determined, will apply from December.

title: Ukraine Uncovers Crime Ring Allegedly Shielded by Officials
content: Ukraine's National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office (SAP) uncovered an alleged criminal organization involving at least 12 people, including serving senior officials from Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), the Prosecutor General's Office and the National Police. NABU and SAP announced Thursday that five alleged members had been formally notified of suspicion, including senior SBU and police officials whose names were not disclosed. Investigators said the group provided protection to fraudulent call centers targeting Ukrainians and foreigners, as well as operations involving illegal drug sales and the production of counterfeit cigarettes and foreign currency. The organization allegedly used corrupt connections within law enforcement to shield its activities and was involved in planned attacks, kidnappings and assaults.

title: Mélenchon’s mission for his young fans: Debate boomers on Facebook
content:
PARIS — Jean-Luc Mélenchon’s campaign has a plan for winning over older French voters: get his young supporters to sign up for Facebook to talk to their parents.

Mélenchon, 75, may be the oldest candidate in next spring’s race to replace Emmanuel Macron. But his progressive platform and call for a civic revolution have made him a hit with younger voters, who are more likely to scroll through TikTok and Snapchat than through the old-school social network.

“We’re strong [on every other social media platform],” said Antoine Léaument, who handles the Mélenchon campaign’s communication operations. “Facebook is one of the places where the digital battle could be decisive.”

More than 40% of voters younger than 35 plan to vote for Mélenchon, according to a recent Cluster17 poll commissioned by POLITICO. That figure drops to 14% or less across the age brackets over 50 — groups that, if they use social media at all, tend to favor Facebook over its newer rivals.

According to Médiamétrie, France’s leading audience measurement company, platforms like Instagram and Snapchat have 35% more daily users than Facebook among 15-to-24-year-olds.

Vaikka omaisten roolin lisääminen herättää joskus kritiikkiä, moni meistä haluaisi auttaa ikääntyviä vanhempiaan paljon nykyistä enemmän. Lapset ja läheiset voisivat auttaa ikääntyneitä asumaan omassa kodissaan pidempään, jos nykyinen työelämä antaisi siihen riittävästi tukea.

title: Ulkomailla haettavien passi- ja henkilökorttihakemusten käsittelyyn esitetään muutoksia
content:
Ulkomailla haettavien passien ja henkilökorttien myöntämistä koskeva päätöksenteko esitetään siirrettäväksi Suomen edustustoilta ulkoministeriölle. Valtioneuvosto antoi eduskunnalle asiaa koskevan esityksen 5.11.2026. Lakimuutosten on tarkoitus tulla voimaan syksyllä 2027.

Esityksen mukaan ulkomailla oleskelevien Suomen kansalaisten passi- ja henkilökorttihakemuksia koskeva päätöksenteko keskitettäisiin Suomen edustustoilta ulkoministeriölle.

Suomen edustustot vastaanottaisivat jatkossakin passi- ja henkilökorttihakemuksia ulkomailla nykyiseen tapaan. Passi- ja henkilökorttitehtäviä voisivat hoitaa myös Suomen edustustoon työsuhteessa olevat henkilöt. Heidän kelpoisuudestaan, tehtävistään ja rikosoikeudellisesta virkavastuustaan säädettäisiin laissa.

Passilakiin ja henkilökorttilakiin lisättäisiin säännökset siitä, että Suomen edustustoissa passia varten jätettyjä sormenjälkiä voitaisiin hyödyntää henkilökortin hakemiseen ja päinvastoin.

Lisäksi henkilökorttilakia muutettaisiin siten, että alaikäisen henkilökorttia voisi hakea myös ulkomailla.

Passi- ja henkilökorttilainsäädännön Suomen kunniakonsulaatteja koskevat säännökset ajantasaistettaisiin ja selkeytettäisiin.

title: The Atlanticist Generation Leaves Congress
content:
America’s midterms have accelerated the departure of the Atlanticist generation, the lawmakers who built and defended transatlantic coalitions in the decades after the Cold War. With some retiring and others being swept out, the bipartisan coalition that kept Europe and Ukraine high on Congress’s agenda is now much thinner.

The champions for Ukraine and the US-European alliance who did not run for re-election include Senators Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Mitch McConnell (R-KY), and John Cornyn (R-TX); along with representatives Mike McCaul (R-TX) and Don Bacon (R-NE); and Speaker Emerita Nancy Pelosi (D-CA). Their international relationships, decades of experience, and political skills will go with them when the new Congress arrives in January.

title: Trains are still safe
content: Last week's horrific rail accident in Spain was the second such accident in the country within the past year. Those two crashes have already killed more passengers than in the deadly year of 2013, when 97 passengers died in train accidents, according to Eurostat. The number of major rail accidents and fatalities has generally declined in Europe since 1980 – despite a small uptick in recent years. Trains remain one of the safest modes of transport. As a train passenger, your risk of dying in a rail accident is one third that of a bus or coach passenger and very similar to that of a commercial aircraft passenger. By comparison, car occupants are around 40 times more likely to die than train passengers travelling the same distance.

title: Tech barons cozied up to Trump. What will they do in newly blue America?
content:
Democrats’ success was helped by popular anger over tech, AI and the super rich – life for billionaires could become much more difficult

The photo of Silicon Valley centibillionaires at Donald Trump’s inauguration – Musk, Bezos and Zuckerberg, front row and side by side – now looks like a hitlist for a blue Congress hellbent on making life difficult for billionaires.

The picture symbolized at the time the bending of the knee by the richest men in the world to its most powerful, a symbiosis of the ultra-rich. Already unfathomably wealthy, Silicon Valley tycoons believed a Maga-sized public shift to the right would enrich them even more. It did. For several years, while Trump seemed an everlasting kingmaker and AI’s expansion seemed unstoppable, their fortunes ballooned to values beyond comprehension. Elon Musk’s surpassed $1tn.

title: SafeSport Will Now Alert Schools, Clubs if Coaches Sanctioned for Abuse Continue to Work With Kids
content:
The U.S. Center for SafeSport is taking steps to stop coaches banned over allegations of sexual abuse from working with children, part of an initiative that the organization said it is launching because of reporting by ProPublica and The Washington Post about gaps in the child protection system in youth sports.

Charged by Congress with investigating allegations of sexual abuse in sports, SafeSport has the power to suspend or permanently bar coaches from contact with athletes and place their names on a public disciplinary list. But the center has authority only over the country’s national sports governing bodies, which are overseen by the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee. Elementary and high schools, colleges and many independent youth sports leagues are not required to follow SafeSport’s bans, though some opt to do so. Parents and other caregivers only know if a coach has been sanctioned if they check the list.

SafeSport’s new initiative encourages people to find and report banned coaches who are continuing to work with children, SafeSport said, with a publicity initiative that includes a video with its CEO.

title: The EU’s next WPS plan must act on tech, not just mention it
content:
The EU is drafting its next action plan on Women, Peace and Security, and technology will inevitably be part of it. The review of 122 national and regional action plans conducted by the Gender in Geopolitics Institute shows how that usually goes: technology is named as a threat, answered with awareness campaigns and never regulated. The EU can do better.

Technology has entered Women, Peace and Security (WPS) national action plans (NAP) fast: before 2018, none treated it as a security issue, but since 2025, 77 per cent do. Yet naming is not acting. Cybersecurity appears in 24 plans, but only 13 take concrete measures. Hybrid threats are mentioned in the plans of Croatia, Finland, Romania, Serbia and NATO, but no country acts on them. Not one technology measure has a target, a baseline or a budget. WPS plans have discovered technology, but they treat it as a danger to women that awareness campaigns can manage. They do not treat it as a power to be governed.

title: Why do blind people and musicians hear pitch better? New research suggests they have less internal noise
content:
People who have lived most of their lives blind often have extraordinary hearing abilities. In new research published in the Journal of Neuroscience, my colleagues and I discovered that this ability arises from how their auditory systems are able to more consistently and reliably process sounds compared with people who aren’t blind. And interestingly, sighted musicians seem to enhance their hearing through a similar mechanism.

Hearing is a complicated process. It involves many stages, starting from how the ears detect sounds and going all the way up to how the brain extracts meaningful information from those sounds.

Different mechanisms are involved, too. You can get better at hearing by being more selective or more consistent. Think of writing the letter “A.” You can practice to make your “A” either more distinguishable from “B” or look more similar to other “A’s” every time you write it. The latter is called internal noise – how consistently your auditory system responds to the same sound over time. The less internal noise you have, the more reliably you can tell similar sounds apart.

title: In the UK, Face Sitting Porn Might Land You in Jail
content:
“I adore breath play. I love being strangled, suffocated and drowned, and I love strangling and suffocating others. Waterboarding: that’s my favourite,” Melissa Todd, a UK-based writer and sex worker, told me. “Many women do: it really isn’t only horrid men forcing us to do these dreadful depraved acts. Interrupting oxygen supply produces the most intense sensation of euphoria. I enjoy it in my private life, and I offer it in sessions too.” 

Starting tomorrow, she and anyone else in the UK distributing or possessing this type of content, even if it’s just recorded in the privacy of their homes and not for sale on a porn site, could face up to five years in prison. The maximum penalty for possession is “two years’ imprisonment for pornography that depicts strangulation or suffocation, or penetrative sexual activity between certain relatives,” according to the law, and “three years’ imprisonment for pornography depicting sexual activity involving a person who is, or is pretending to be, under 16,” with five years as the maximum penalty for publication of all of the above.

title: Hong Kong: Joshua Wong Gets Nearly 10 More Years in Prison
content:
(Tokyo) – The Hong Kong High Court on November 5, 2026, sentenced Joshua Wong, a well-known democracy activist, to 10 years in prison on baseless national security charges, Human Rights Watch said today. Two months of the sentence will run concurrently with his current national security sentence. Wong has been in custody since November 2020, when he was 24, and faces imprisonment until late 2036, when he will be 40.

The Hong Kong government should immediately and unconditionally release Wong. Foreign governments should denounce the sentences against him and other wrongfully detained pro-democracy activists and impose targeted sanctions on officials responsible for Hong Kong’s growing repression.

“The harsh sentence on baseless charges against Joshua Wong is cruel and unjust,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. “Young people promoting social change are an asset for any vibrant society, but the Hong Kong government puts them behind bars.”

title: Hackers Steal Estimated 118 Million Euros in Cyberattack on French Bank
content:
French banking group Crédit Mutuel Arkéa suffered a sophisticated cyberattack that allegedly siphoned an estimated 118 million euros ($132.44 million) from its corporate accounts, though the institution stated that client assets were untouched.

In a Wednesday public statement and a subsequent update, the bank explained that hackers infiltrated its systems through a third-party service provider's platform. The attackers bypassed client accounts entirely, using Crédit Mutuel Arkéa’s proprietary accounts to transfer funds to other banks. The stolen money was then potentially converted into cryptocurrency on specialized platforms, the bank said.

Addressing media reports that 118 million euros were stolen, the bank did not confirm the exact figure but validated the "order of magnitude."

title: EU budget battle paralyzes Brussels on AI chips, the Arctic and agriculture
content:
BRUSSELS — Europe’s push to accelerate AI chip production and plan to strengthen its Arctic presence are among the key EU policy files caught in the logjam of Brussels’ seven-year budget standoff.

European policymakers say they can’t move forward on their files without sufficient visibility on proposals linked to EU funding, as the negotiating impasse over the size of the EU’s 2028-2034 budget means financial allocations after next year are unknown.

“There’s an increase in sectoral legislation with objectives that require multiannual budgetary commitments,” said a person involved in talks on the EU budget, who was granted anonymity to discuss closed-door negotiations. “But the budget talks are disconnected from the policy discussions.”

EU governments are racing to find a deal among themselves over the total size of the money pot by the end of the year. The so-called frugal countries pushing for major budget cuts — Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Sweden, Denmark and Finland — have publicly said that a proposal by the Irish presidency of the Council of the EU envisioning €159 billion cuts doesn’t go far enough.
snippet: BRUSSELS — Europe’s push to accelerate AI chip production and plan to strengthen its Arctic presence are among the key EU policy files caught in the logjam of Brussels’ seven-year budget standoff.

title: Not too small to matter
content:
Big states cannot cover it all. Smaller European states are stepping in, creating influence through niche politics. Ultimately, the argument that smaller states need to identify WPS areas where they can bring real added value has the potential to create influence based on outside-the-box thinking.

The Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda is often discussed through the lens of major European powers, such as the United Kingdom, France and Germany. And although smaller European states, especially the Nordic countries, are recognised as crucial WPS actors, the contributions of other countries, such as Austria, Ireland and Czechia, remain comparatively under the radar. Sustaining the WPS agenda requires stronger alliances and broader coalitions. It is therefore worth examining what smaller states can contribute when using their niche. The relevance lies not simply in filling gaps left by larger powers, but in how smaller states can use their specific expertise to foster impactful WPS practices.

title: The Binance hack exploited familiar weaknesses – all organisations should learn from it
content:
Hackers have stolen around US$6.3 billion (£4.7 billion) from the cryptocurrency exchange Binance, most of which was taken in under an hour. According to Binance, the attack exploited systems and individuals with the authority to carry out transactions involving such large sums.

Such vulnerabilities exist everywhere; statistics show that people and the systems they directly use, including their personal computers, remain a top target for cybercriminals. All organisations could therefore learn lessons from this attack.

The Binance theft took place on the evening of October 29, 2026. The Binance attack netted four times the amount stolen in the previous biggest cryptocurrency theft, on the Bybit exchange in February 2025.

Private keys, used to authorise spending or withdrawal from crypto-wallets, are a known vulnerability. But Binance found no evidence these were leaked. An initial statement from the exchange pointed to a compromised laptop belonging to an engineer. This gave the attacker access to the internal system that processes withdrawal requests.

title: What makes music truly ‘Russian’? The forgotten debate between Tchaikovsky and his star pupil
content:
What makes a piece of music Russian? A folk tune, a church melody, or simply the fact that the composer was born in Russia? For 19th-century composer Sergei Taneyev (1856-1915), the answer was complicated. He wanted Russian composers to develop a musical voice of their own. But he believed they could do so by learning from composers elsewhere in Europe.

By the time Taneyev began his career, the world of classical music in Russia was expanding. Musical life, which had previously been centred on the imperial court and aristocratic families, increasingly came to include public concerts and new institutions for training professional musicians. Conservatoires opened in St Petersburg in 1862 and in Moscow in 1866, where teaching methods developed in various European countries were employed.

Svenska litteratursällskapet i Finland (SLS) avaa haettavaksi useita uusia tukimuotoja vuodesta 2027 alkaen. Tuotantotuki ammattimaisille kustantajille laadukkaan ja monipuolisen kirjallisuustarjonnan ylläpitämiseksi sekä ruotsinkielisen kirjallisuuden monimuotoisuuden edistämiseksi Suomessa. title: UK Expands Human Rights Sanctions Regime
content:
The UK has significantly expanded its Global Human Rights Sanctions Regime, allowing the government, for the first time, to impose targeted sanctions on individuals and entities involved in war crimes. The new powers were approved by parliament yesterday.

The previous framework, adopted in 2020, did not allow for such sanctions, providing, instead, for targeted sanctions only for certain serious human rights violations of the right to life, freedom from torture, and freedom from slavery and forced labor. Under the new rules, the government can also target those responsible for serious violations of international humanitarian law, obstruction of humanitarian assistance, and violations of the right to liberty and security of person.

This is an important step that means the UK can impose consequences for atrocities committed around the world. Although Foreign Secretary, Ed Miliband, announced the change in September while laying out measures to address Israel’s unlawful settlement expansion in the West Bank, the powers can also be used against those responsible for war crimes anywhere.

title: Russia denies involvement in fridge hacks across Europe
content:
A spokesperson for the Kremlin denied on Thursday that Russia had any involvement in the cyberattacks affecting supermarket refrigerators, calling the allegations “absurd.”

Dmitry Peskov said accusations of Russian involvement in the attacks are “unfounded,” according to reports in Russian media. These allegations are “becoming a persistent trend in European countries,” he added.

Supermarket refrigerators have been hacked in multiple European countries over the past few weeks, forcing retailers to throw away thawing fresh and frozen food. The attacks also hit French blood banks, though the country’s blood collection service said its supplies were not affected.

While pro-Russian hacker groups claimed the attacks on Wednesday, it is notoriously difficult to attribute a cyberattack to a specific actor definitively, and those groups quickly deleted the claims, according to the BBC.

title: Elon Musk’s nearly half a billion dollars in midterms spending was a flop
content:
The tech billionaire set spending record as he poured $446m into campaigns for failed Republican candidates

Elon Musk set a record for election spending this year after pouring nearly half a billion dollars into backing Republicans in the US midterm elections. It turned out to be a poor investment.

The SpaceX and Tesla CEO contributed at least $446m to Republican-aligned Super Pacs and groups over the course of the elections, specifically targeting several key Senate races in an effort to help the Trump administration retain Republican control of Congress. He outdid his own 2024 spending of nearly $290m. Yet as Democrats swept to power across the country on Tuesday night, it became clear that Musk would get nearly nothing in return for his hundreds of millions in spending.

title: Young men and Latino voters helped drive the Democrats’ blue wave. Why did they abandon Trump?
content:
The young men and Hispanic and Latino voters who helped propel Donald Trump to his presidential victory in 2024 swung sharply towards the Democrats in the midterm elections, contributing to the historic defeat for Republicans.

Charles Hunt, an associate professor of political science at Boise State University in Idaho, tells The Conversation Weekly podcast that the results suggest weakened support for Trump and his MAGA movement among these key groups of voters.

Hispanic and Latino voters “swung heavily towards Trump in 2024”, Hunt says. But midterm results in Florida, Texas and elsewhere “are showing these voters just slingshotting completely in the other direction,” he explains, citing early exit polls and analysis by The New York Times.

Not just back towards where they were in, say, 2018 or 2020 in terms of support for Democrats, but past that – being more supportive of folks like James Talarico in Texas than they have been of any Democrat in the last 20 years.

That’s really, really significant, especially since that’s a growing part of the electorate.

title: Republicans Learn X Is the Echo Chamber
content:
There's a BlazeTV YouTube video whose thumbnail shows the presenter with his arms around Anakin Skywalker and a gender-flipped Draco Malfoy called Malfoid. “Total Chud Victory?” It says. The video's title: “Young Right is Reclaiming Culture and Liberals Are Mad About it.”

BlazeTV posted the video on November 2, the day before Democrats swept the midterms and started a political realignment in America so overwhelming that Republicans lost control of all the most powerful state positions in Texas.

The video is a profound misreading of the political and cultural moment. It reminded me of stories of the Bolsheviks seizing the Winter Palace to discover tarot card playing courtiers who had no idea a revolution was happening in the streets.

The American version was watching defense contractor Palmer Lucky dress up like Harry Potter on Halloween while standing next to his Malfoid wife. And it was Elon Musk — who spent roughly half a billion on the election only to see his chosen candidates fail — posting an AI generated picture of Anakin Skywalker sitting at the head of a happy fascist Star Wars family two days before the midterms.

title: ‘Stop using US tech’: EU lawmaker says Starlink service cutoff led to deaths
content:
“Stop using U.S. tech. That’s my message,” Finnish EPP lawmaker Aura Salla declared Thursday at the European Pulse Seminar.

In an interview with POLITICO, Salla argued that last month’s speed cap on the SpaceX military Starshield service in Ukraine was “yet another example of a kill switch,” which in this case led directly to battlefield deaths.

“We are losing lives in Ukraine. It’s about our defense, because defense is technology.”

Salla issued her stark warning as a pushback against Brussels’ growing focus on AI adoption over building frontier models in Europe. In her Sept. 16 State of the Union address, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said: “We do not need to be the ones who develop the frontier technology to be the ones who draw the greatest value from it.”

Salla argued that Europe needs frontier models to have “any room in these negotiations,” over the direct of artificial development and safety. Leading French frontier lab Mistral has likewise warned that Europe will be shut out from shaping AI without a player leading development of the most advance models.

title: Europe: Get Satellites or Get Throttled
content:
European powers must urgently break Elon Musk’s near-monopoly over military communications. It won’t be easy. It won’t be cheap. It won’t happen fast. But it’s necessary to ensure no one man can repeat the trillionaire’s treatment of Ukraine in early October, when he throttled Ukraine’s access to the Starlink and Starshield satellite systems now central to its military operations.

Starlink is a commercial satellite communications service, with Starshield a more capable military version. Both belong to Musk’s SpaceX. Ukraine — and many other Western powers, for that matter — relies on them for an array of vital military functions. They connect troops to their headquarters and drones to their operators.

Overnight and without warning in mid-October, thousands of satellite terminals failed in Ukraine. Operators discovered that SpaceX had imposed a speed limit of approximately 160 kmh (100 mph) or slower. Above that speed, a drone couldn’t connect to its operator. Many of the faster drones, including interceptor drones that Ukraine uses to defeat Russia’s own attack drones, couldn’t function.

title: Culture gains a stronger name and place in the European Parliament’s Horizon Europe compromise
content:
Culture Action Europe is proud to be part of the Name Place Fund coalition, which brings together culture and research organisations advocating for stronger support for culture in Horizon Europe and the European Competitiveness Fund. The coalition welcomes the cross-party compromise text on Horizon Europe 2028-2034 negotiated in the European Parliament. 

It was prepared by rapporteurs Christian Ehler (EPP) and René Repasi (S&D) together with the shadow rapporteurs. The compromise is scheduled for a vote in Parliament’s Industry, Research and Energy (ITRE) Committee on 10 November. This text will be the starting point for the Parliament’s negotiations with the Commission and the Council. 

After long negotiations, culture, creativity and artistic research finally have a more prominent place in the future EU research and innovation programme, signalling an important shift in how the role of arts and culture in research and innovation is understood.

title: US midterms delivered a blow to tech’s AI ambitions
content:
There’s no question the US midterms elections delivered a blow to Donald Trump. The Democrats took not just the House and Senate back from the Republicans, but won a wave of governor’s races across the country — including in states it would’ve previously been hard to imagine a Democrat winning.

But it wasn’t just Trump who lost. The tech industry and its ambitions to cover the country in hyperscale data centers to power generative AI were potentially even bigger losers than the orange man himself.

It didn’t matter that Elon Musk shelled out over $400 million to try to save Republicans as polling increasingly suggested a wipeout was coming, especially in his chosen home of Texas, or that crypto and AI companies deployed millions more on races across the country. An NBC News exit poll still found 56% of voters said AI and data centers were “crucial or a major factor” in their vote for Congress. And it showed in the results.

title: EU governments call it ‘simplification,’ but their Data Omnibus deal considerably weakens our rights
content:
EU governments have agreed on their position on the Digital Omnibus, retaining changes that threaten fundamental rights to privacy and data protection. With negotiations moving to the European Parliament, MEPs must reject the proposed weakening of GDPR safeguards for AI and pseudonymised data, protect individual rights, and defend ePrivacy against new tracking exemptions. Genuine simplification should make our rights easier to exercise and enforce, not give companies more freedom to exploit our data.

title: Launch of European.Social: the movement for the European open social web
content:
Today, November 4, the European.Social movement was officially launched in Berlin with a celebratory event at the location of Wikimedia Deutschland. The movement takes on a legal form in the European Social Association e.V., which was also established today. The association will coordinate the movement for open, decentralised and interoperable social media in Europe. More than 150 organisations and almost 700 individuals support the initiative, including PublicSpaces.

European.Social began as a shared manifesto, launched on 5 June 2026 at the PublicSpaces Conference with 12 founding signatories – including PublicSpaces. Since then, the movement has grown with 40 builders, 14 communities, 86 organisations and 676 individuals. Together, they are building open social infrastructure for Europe from a set of shared values and principles like democracy, digital autonomy and open source.

title: Burning questions about burning trash
content: Depending on where you live, your waste can take several routes. About half of the waste in the EU gets recycled or composted, the rest ends up either in a landfill or a giant furnace. Burning waste in specialised plants can transform that waste into energy – something that Europe constantly needs more of. Sounds like a win-win? Not so fast. Though incinerating waste reduces the amount sent to landfills and the resulting methane emissions, burning generates ashes, metals, and large quantities of CO₂. “Incinerators are among the most carbon-intensive energy sources in some countries,” Janek Vähk, a policy manager at Zero Waste Europe, told us. “Because these plants are less efficient in energy generation, the greenhouse gas emissions per unit of electricity are almost double those of fossil gas power.” Modern waste-to-energy plants, such as Vienna's colourful Spittelau plant, can limit negative environmental impacts with advanced filtering systems. They work with the city's municipal waste management, which recovers recyclable material from the slag and ash left after incineration, Martin Meyrath from Wien Energie told The European Correspondent. title: Vermont Was Supposed to Get an Audit of Its Lake Champlain Cleanup. It Never Happened.
content:
This summer, Vermont’s Clean Water Board celebrated a milestone: Over the past decade, the state has invested nearly a billion dollars to clean up its polluted streams, rivers and lakes. The vast majority of that money has gone toward Lake Champlain.

“I think that’s something to be extremely proud of,” said Douglas Farnham, the board’s chair.

Vermont was supposed to get an independent evaluation of what it has gotten for all that money. But that study was never done.

A decade ago, Vermont lawmakers mandated that the board submit an audit from an outside environmental consultant to determine whether the projects the state had invested in to improve water quality were working. The audit also was meant to examine whether the state’s agriculture and natural resource agencies are doing enough to enforce water quality regulations on farms, which are the biggest source of phosphorus in Lake Champlain.

Seven Days and ProPublica have teamed up to investigate the cleanup of Lake Champlain. Have you been affected by this issue? We’d like to hear from you.

title: The 2027 Mark Palmer Prize: Call for Nominations
content:
Freedom House is now accepting nominations for the 2027 Mark Palmer Prize, inviting individuals and organizations around the world to put forward candidates whose work exemplifies the important role of diplomacy in supporting democratic movements and defending fundamental freedoms.

The award takes its name from the late Mark Palmer, a longtime Freedom House trustee and US ambassador to Hungary from 1986 to 1990. In 1989, as the Cold War was coming to a close, Palmer boldly joined civil society and the Hungarian democratic opposition to support the country’s transition to democracy.
 
The Mark Palmer Prize has been awarded to diplomats and international civil servants from around the world, including Georgia, Peru, the Czech Republic, Lithuania, Mongolia, Sweden, Canada, Uruguay, and the United States. The prize is made possible through the generosity of the Mark and Sushma Palmer Legacy Fund, established by Dr. Sushma Palmer in loving memory of her late husband and former Freedom House trustee and vice chairman Ambassador Mark Palmer. 

Nomination Form

Criteria 

The award winner must be a current or former diplomat or official serving in an intergovernmental institution.

title: The scandals and suspects surrounding Flávio Bolsonaro, according to the Brazilian press
content:
After being defeated in the elections, the senator fled to the US with his family

Originally published on Global Voices

Art by Global Voices with Canva Pro. Photo by the Brazilian Senate. Fair use.

Forty-eight hours after losing the runoff in Brazil to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Flávio Bolsonaro, former president Jair Bolsonaro’s eldest son, a senator representing Rio de Janeiro, fled to the United States. From there, where his brother Eduardo, a former congressman, has lived since February 2025, he continues to challenge the results of the election he lost by 4.4 million votes, as attested by the Electoral Court (TSE), the Organization of American States (OAS), and other right-led governments in the region.

Upon landing in Miami, Flávio published a letter proclaiming himself “the true president of Brazil” and “president-elect of Brazil.” After 22 minutes — and a demand from the US Department of State — he retracted to “the leader of Brazil.”

title: HERITΛGE delivers Seasonal School on heritage adaptation to climate change
content:
Working with Prof. Brimblecombe

How can climate projections help heritage professionals decide which monument needs attention first? And what does adaptation mean for a mountain community whose landscape and traditions are threatened by recurring wildfires? These were among the questions that heritage professionals and researchers brought to Athens for the first Seasonal School of the European Partnership for Resilient Cultural Heritage (RCH).

The Heritage Management Organization (HERITΛGE) delivered the school, Heritage Adaptation to Climate Change, from 5 to 15 October 2026. More than 400 applications were filed from around the world. Fourteen participants attended in person at the European Parliament’s Europa Experience in Athens, and more than 100 took part online. The in-person participants were selected from candidates nominated by states participating in RCH. They represented 13 countries, with two participants from Spain and one each from Belgium, Croatia, Egypt, Finland, Greece, Italy, Lithuania, Malta, the Netherlands, Portugal, Romania and the United Kingdom.

title: OPINION: Our Insignificance
content:
By Jonathan Power*

LUND, Sweden | 4 November 2026 (IDN) — “Suppose aliens existed, and that some had been watching our planet for its entire forty-five million centuries, what would they have seen? Over most of that vast time-span, Earth’s appearance altered very gradually. Continents drifted; ice-cover waxed and waned; successive species emerged, evolved and became extinct.

“But just in a tiny sliver of Earth’s history—the last hundred centuries—the patterns of vegetation altered much faster than before. This signalled the start of agriculture—and then urbanization.”

We are at the very end of that “sliver”.

So begins a book by Martin Rees, Britain’s former Astronomer Royal, On the Future: Prospects for Humanity.

There is much in this short, very readable book—the disturbing, sometimes positive, sometimes negative, future of biotech, artificial intelligence, global warming, medicine, ageing, communications, nuclear energy, weapons development, sustainability, agricultural research, poverty and employment—but its centrepiece is astronomy.

title: Kroatialainen Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić viettää eläkepäiviä tipujen ja älypuhelimen kanssa ja muistelee hyvällä Titon aikoja
content:
Autioituneiden rakennusten ikkunoista kurkottaa vihreinä rehottavia puiden oksia. Tienviertä reunustavat talot, joiden katot ovat romahtamaisillaan. Osa taloista on jäänyt keskeneräisiksi, jotkut seisovat tyhjillään, toisissa asutaan yhä.

Pohjois-Kroatian maaseutu on paikoittain karua katseltavaa: muuttoliike kaupunkeihin ja ulkomaille käy kuumana samalla, kun kylät pysyvät vaivoin pystyssä iäkkäiden asukkaiden ja satunnaisten paluumuuttajien ansiosta. Yksi tällaisista on 77-vuotias Klara Bošnjak Fabijanić.

”Tiesin aina, että eläkkeelle jäätyäni muuttaisin takaisin omaan pieneen kylääni.”

Kitinä on kova, kun Bošnjak Fabijanić nostaa sisäpihan kaivosta ämpärillisen kukkienkasteluvettä Unkarin rajalla, Drava-joen eteläpuolella, sijaitsevassa Podravska Moslavinan kylässä.

Sisällä olisi nykyisin myös juoksevaa vettä, mutta Bošnjak Fabijanić käyttää piha-askareisiin mieluummin samaa kaivoa, josta hän on nostanut vedet vuosikymmenten ajan.

Podravska Moslavina on Bošnjak Fabijanićin kotikylä ja koti, jossa hän asuu, hänen lapsuudenkotinsa.

Nyt paikalla on myös hänen tyttärensä, Marija Fabijani.

”Tämä paikka tuo minulle rauhan”, hän sanoo katsellen raukeana ympärilleen.

title: NASA’s Swift telescope has burned up, months after a robot sent to save it failed – here’s why it’s so hard to boost a satellite
content:
NASA’s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory took its last look at the sky on Oct. 20, 2026, while orbiting about 171 miles (275 kilometers) above Earth. NASA ended the telescope’s mission three days later, because Swift had sunk so low that drag from the thin air there meant its telescopes couldn’t hold steady. The telescope reentered the atmosphere on Nov. 4 above the North Sumatra region of Indonesia and largely burned up, an abrupt ending to two decades spent observing powerful cosmic explosions.

Swift’s reentry comes after a failed rescue mission in the summer of 2026. LINK, a commercial robotic spacecraft sent to raise Swift into a safer orbit, reentered Earth’s atmosphere in September. The machine designed to save a falling satellite burned up first.

As a Ph.D. candidate in aerospace engineering, I know that rescuing satellites is hard. I research how spacecraft approach and capture satellites, including objects that tumble uncontrollably.

Swift’s loss points to a new hazard for the young industry that repairs, refuels and moves spacecraft around in orbit. If something goes wrong, the spacecraft doing the rescuing can become another problem.

title: Pekingin pitkä käsi – Toimitusketjujen läpinäkyvyyttä koetellaan jälleen, kun Kiina rakentaa ekstraterritoriaalista sääntelyään
content:
Kiina on pitkään arvostellut Yhdysvaltojen tapaa ulottaa pakotteensa, vientirajoituksensa ja sääntelynsä maan rajojen ulkopuolelle. Nyt Peking pyrkii rakentamaan omaa “pitkää kättään” ja sitä kautta vaikuttamaan yritysten ja yksilöiden toimintaan myös omien rajojensa ulkopuolella. Ennen kaikkea hallinnon tarkoituksena on vaikeuttaa tai estää ulkomaisten toimitusketjuja koskevien vaatimusten toimeenpanoa silloin, kun niiden katsotaan vahingoittavan Kiinan etuja. 

Kiinan valtioneuvoston keväällä 2026 antamat asetukset 834 ja 835 ovat uusi ase suurvaltojen välisessä kauppasodassa. Asetus 834 (“toimitusketjujen turvallisuusasetus”) antaa Kiinan viranomaisille valtuudet seurata, suojata ja tarvittaessa puuttua toimitusketjuihin liittyviin riskeihin. Asetus 835 (“ulkomaiden ekstraterritoriaalisen lainkäytön vastainen asetus”) puolestaan mahdollistaa sen, että Kiina voi tunnistaa tiettyjä ulkomaisia lakeja tai viranomaistoimia ”epäasianmukaisiksi” ja kieltää niiden noudattamisen.

title: American Voters Overwhelmingly Reject AI Data Centers
content:
People across America rejected data centers during last night’s midterm election. Proposals related to data centers were explicitly on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states. People voted against data centers in 38 of them and counting. Six cities voted to ban data centers outright and 12 put limits on the amount of megawatts such buildings could draw. In addition to specific ballot measures, candidates who supported data centers lost across the country.

One of the most striking repudiations of pro data center politicians was in Texas, where Gregg Abbott lost a bid for a fourth term as governor. Abbott had made Texas a data center friendly place. The state has more than 300 working data centers and there are plans to double that number. “Texas is the epicenter of AI development,” Abbott said in 2025 at a press conference with Google CEO Sundar Pichai. “We must ensure that America remains at the forefront of the AI revolution, and Texas is the place where that can happen.” He went on to accept more than $9 million from data center-related donors.

title: Belgium: ‘Divisive’ migration home raids law must be voted down by parliament
content:
Ahead of the vote in Belgian Federal Parliament on Thursday 5 November on whether to allow police raids on people’s homes for migration control purposes, including homes of people who may be hosting undocumented migrants, Dinushika Dissanayake the Deputy Regional Director of Amnesty International said:

“These proposals which allow for home raids are bound to sow fear and division. The bill before Belgium’s parliament gives police vast powers to enter people’s homes for migration control purposes, between the hours of 5am and 9pm and irrespective of whether children are present.

“This would not only cause a serious intrusion into people’s private and family life but also the bill fails to provide effective ways to appeal or challenge these decisions.

“Belgium has a strong tradition of showing solidarity towards migrant communities, with many people opening their doors and homes to offer beds, food and support – as is their prerogative. This will discourage people from doing so in future.

“These disproportionate powers are another cruel and coercive tool to create an increasingly hostile environment for migrants in Europe and for those showing solidarity with them.

title: Q&A: What is the Brazil-led ‘deforestation roadmap’?
content:
• What is a deforestation ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the roadmap say about reducing deforestation?
  • Why did some countries not sign onto the roadmap at COP30?
  • What are the barriers to implementing a deforestation roadmap? 

    • On 3 November, the Brazilian presidency of the COP30 climate talks released its long-awaited “roadmap” on ending deforestation. 

    Ahead of the Belém summit, Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva made a call for a “roadmap” to halt and reverse deforestation.

    Although this voluntary roadmap was outside the COP’s official agenda, it snowballed into a rallying point at the “Amazon” COP.

    Some 93 countries called for a reference to a new roadmap for ending deforestation to be part of COP30’s formal negotiated outcome.

    However, at the end of the summit, the COP30 presidency announced that there was not the consensus needed for the deforestation roadmap to be part of the final text – but that Brazil would work to create a voluntary roadmap outside of the UN climate process.

    This call was answered by 18 countries and four negotiating blocs that offered their inputs on the roadmap, along with scores of NGOs, research centres and other groups.

title: "Over a Decade of Organizing": Keisha Lance Bottoms Elected First Black Woman Governor in U.S. History
content: Black voters in Georgia on Tuesday said, “Not today, Satan,” according to professor Carol Anderson, professor of African American studies at Emory University. Despite the Trump administration’s efforts to disenfranchise Black voters in the South this election cycle and the Supreme Court’s gutting of the Voting Rights Act, she says there was “massive turnout” that propelled Democrats to victory. Former Atlanta Mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms defeated billionaire Republican healthcare executive Rick Jackson, becoming the first Black woman ever elected governor in the United States. Incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff also handily won his bid for reelection.

title: We’re Asking the Ninth Circuit to Hold Reverse Location Warrants Categorically Unconstitutional
content: Yesterday, along with the ACLU, EFF filed an amicus brief in the Ninth Circuit court of appeals in United States v. Spurlock, a case involving a “tower dump” warrant. These overbroad warrants require cellular providers to turn over location data about every phone in a given area at a given time. This is the first such case to be heard by a federal appeals court since the US Supreme Court ruled this summer that highly similar “geofence” warrants are searches under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

title: Uusi julkaisu: Digitaalinen teknologia muokkaa perhesuhteita
content:
Family Relationships in the Digital Era -kirja kokoaa yhteen johtavia tutkijoita tarkastelemaan, miten digitaaliset teknologiat ovat kietoutuneet perhe-elämään, ja voivat sekä yhdistää että etäännyttää perhesuhteita.

Kirja ei ota kantaa siihen, onko teknologia perhe-elämälle hyväksi vai haitaksi, vaan kokoaa yhteen viimeisen reilun vuosikymmenen tutkimustulokset ja tarjoaa näin monipuolisen, tutkimukseen perustuvan tilannekuvan aiheesta. Teos luo katsauksen satoihin tutkimuksiin ja niihin perustuen läpileikkaaviksi teemoiksi muodostuu kaksi tärkeää näkökulmaa. Ensinnäkin digitaalinen teknologia on muuttanut perheiden ajankäyttöä ja huomion kohdentumista, mutta samalla laajentanut merkittävästi mahdollisuuksia pitää yhteyttä perheenjäseniin. Toisena merkittävänä teemana teoksen läpi kulkee ymmärrys siitä, että ihmismieli kantaa yhä mukanaan perhe-elämän evolutiivista perintöä nopeasta teknologisesta muutoksesta huolimatta.

title: HP nimittää Emma Walmsleyn toimitusjohtajaksi
content:
PALO ALTO, Kalifornia, 4.11.2026 – HP Inc:n (NYSE: HPQ) hallitus on yksimielisesti nimittänyt Emma Walmsleyn yhtiön toimitusjohtajaksi 4.1.2027 alkaen. Walmsley toimi viimeksi GSK:n toimitusjohtajana, ja hän on ollut Microsoftin hallituksen jäsen seitsemän vuotta. Hän seuraa tehtävässä Bruce Broussardia, joka on toiminut väliaikaisena toimitusjohtajana helmikuusta 2026. Broussard siirtyy samana päivänä hallituksen puheenjohtajaksi Chip Berghin tilalle.

”HP:llä on valtavasti potentiaalia nyt, kun teknologia on tärkeässä murroskohdassa. Tarvitsemme johtajan, joka rakentaa innovaatioperinteemme ja vahvuuksiemme varaan ja muovaa rohkeasti yhtiön tulevaisuutta. Emma on toimitusjohtajana näyttänyt, että hän osaa johtaa suuria organisaatioita ja viedä niitä isojen muutosten läpi. Hänellä on kokemusta ja taitoa koota HP:n liiketoiminnat, osaaminen ja ihmiset yhteen, jotta voimme tarttua mahdollisuuksiin, joita tekoälyn siirtyminen laitteisiin tarjoaa. Tekoäly muuttaa samalla työntekoa ja arkea yhä verkottuneemmassa maailmassa. Tuen häntä mielelläni, kun hän vie HP:n seuraavaan kasvuvaiheeseen”, sanoo väliaikainen toimitusjohtaja Bruce Broussard.

title: The £10,000 refugee tax must be scrapped | Letters
content:
Such a punitive measure will leave people at risk of exploitation and severe poverty, says Mark Joselin of the Refugee Council

Cabinet ministers are right to be worried about the potential impact of the new asylum bill (Mahmood infuriates fellow ministers by failing to reveal impact of UK migration shake-up, 30 October). The proposed refugee tax unfairly punishes refugees by threatening to slap most with a £10,000 tax once they are granted refugee status, a clear breach of the UN refugee convention.

It is aimed at those who arrived with nothing and were not allowed to work while their claims were being assessed, and it ignores the reality that refugees already contribute through the tax system.

title: US: New Congress Should Assert Oversight
content:
(Washington, DC) – The newly elected US Congress should prioritize respect and protection for human rights both within the United States and around the world, Human Rights Watch said today. Voters elected a majority of Democrats to control both the House and the Senate in the November 3, 2026 midterm elections. 

“This newly elected Congress will convene at a critical moment for human rights domestically and globally,” said Michael García Bochenek, interim US program director at Human Rights Watch. “Lawmakers should challenge the Trump administration’s many abuses, embrace the oversight authority provided to Congress, and act decisively to respect, protect, and fulfill human rights.”

title: Młodzi ludzie apelują o nową kulturę pokoju. UNESCO popiera ich postulaty
content:
Podczas 225. sesji Rady Wykonawczej UNESCO, która odbyła się w październiku 2026 roku, poparto „Call by Young People for a New Culture of Peace in the Minds of Women and Men for the 21st Century” – apel młodych ludzi na rzecz budowania nowej kultury pokoju w XXI wieku.

Dokument powstał w wyniku konsultacji przeprowadzonych od lipca do września 2026 roku z udziałem 145 młodych liderów ze 135 krajów. Zawiera postulaty dotyczące większego udziału młodych ludzi w procesach decyzyjnych oraz wzmacniania działań na rzecz pokoju poprzez edukację, naukę, kulturę, ochronę dziedzictwa i odpowiedzialne wykorzystanie nowych technologii.

Ważne miejsce w apelu zajmuje rola kultury i dziedzictwa kulturowego w budowaniu dialogu i wzajemnego zrozumienia. Autorzy podkreślają, że zarówno materialne, jak i niematerialne dziedzictwo kulturowe wymagają skuteczniejszej ochrony, szczególnie w sytuacjach konfliktów i kryzysów. Zwracają również uwagę na znaczenie pamięci, wymiany międzykulturowej i zaangażowania społeczności w budowanie pokojowych relacji.

title: Museum Shop Trends: Five Ideas to Test
content:
Museum shops can introduce visitors to local makers, extend an exhibition’s story and generate income for the institution. They also have to make practical retail decisions about stock, pricing, access and the time available to their teams.

A useful starting point is to choose one change that fits your museum and test it. Better product information, a small local-maker range or clearer online collection options may be more useful than an expensive new retail feature.

Here are five areas to consider when developing a museum shop, with examples and questions to help you decide what is worth trying.

Responsible sourcing starts with details: materials, packaging, manufacturing and the evidence behind the supplier’s claims. A museum shop can help customers understand those details, but it should avoid calling a product sustainable without explaining why.

The British Museum shop provides a concrete example. Its Great Wave foldable tote bag is described as being woven from 100% recycled polyester and is inspired by Hokusai’s print. The product page gives a material specification and a collection connection. That is more useful to a buyer than a broad environmental label.

title: Iraq Jails Ex-Oil Boss for Eight Years Over $119M Kickback Scheme
content:
A high-profile court ruling against a senior former oil official has delivered another warning to Iraq’s political establishment that high office no longer guarantees impunity, an influential lawmaker told OCCRP on Wednesday, as authorities widen an aggressive anti-corruption campaign across the country’s lucrative energy sector.

The verdict sends “a clear message that positions and responsibilities do not grant immunity from accountability,” said Qaisar al-Jorani, a member of parliament’s committee on oil, gas, and natural resources, calling the misappropriation of state wealth a “red line that must not be crossed.”

The ruling, handed down by Iraq’s Criminal Court for Combating Corruption, sentenced Hussein Talib Abboud, the former director general of the State Company for Oil Products Distribution, to eight years in prison and ordered him to repay 55 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $36.2 million).

title: If Fritz Lang’s Iconic Film Metropolis Had a Kraftwerk Soundtrack
content:
The case of the copyright history of Fritz Lang’s influential sci-fi masterpiece Metropolis is as convoluted as the history of its film print. Lang’s vision and his original almost-three-hour cut were doomed to censorship right from the start. The Nazis took out its more socialist scenes. It’s been edited, colorized, put back together and restored. Wikipedia currently lists nine different versions. Similarly, ownership of the film shifted from distributors back to the public domain, then out of it again, once more of the original footage was rediscovered. And then came 2023, when Metropolis once again landed in the public domain, at least in America. Will we see as many legal battles as new remixes and re-scores? Probably a bit of both.

The film’s original orchestral score is available, but many fans also seek out a score more befitting its futurist origins. Something more electronic.

title: Metsola tells MEPs not to rely on AI when drafting laws
content:
European Parliament President Roberta Metsola warned MEPs Wednesday not to be overreliant on AI in decision-making, as the Parliament prepares new guidelines for lawmakers on how to use it.

“Drafting an amendment with the help of AI cannot replace fundamentally the constructive debate with a colleague,” she said at an event on AI use in the Parliament. “Doing legal research with the help of AI cannot ultimately replace the judgment and the critical thinking needed to make a tough decision.”

Metsola said there must be “democratic accountability” in lawmaking and argued that “where AI is used, people should know.”

“No matter how AI may be used in a parliament, the responsibility is still [with] those who are elected,” she said.

Secretary-General Alessandro Chiocchetti said at the same event that Parliament is building its own AI tool for sensitive work, hosted on its internal infrastructure.

As POLITICO reported in July, commercial AI models, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Meta’s Llama, can still be used for less sensitive tasks.

    Tämän syksyn aikana nuoret ovat protestoineet eri puolilla Eurooppaa. Kyse ei ole yhdestä yhtenäisestä liikkeestä, mutta kokemus petetystä tulevaisuuslupauksesta ja sukupolvien välisestä epäoikeudenmukaisuudesta yhdistää nuoria eurooppalaisia sukupolvia. title: Tekijänoikeuskorvaukset nousivat maailmalla ennätykselliseen 15,5 miljardiin euroon
content:
Tekijänoikeuskorvaukset kasvoivat globaalisti 11,3 prosenttia edellisvuodesta. Kasvua vauhdittivat erityisesti korvaukset digitaalisilta alustoilta, jotka muodostavat jo yli 40 prosenttia kaikista korvauksista. Digitaalisten korvausten kasvava merkitys alleviivaa reilujen pelisääntöjen tarvetta tekoälylle ja muille digialustoille.

Viimeisen viiden vuoden aikana luovista sisällöistä maksetut tekijänoikeuskorvaukset ovat olleet tasaisessa kasvussa. Vuonna 2025 korvauksia kerättiin maailmanlaajuisesti ennätykselliset 15,5 miljardia euroa. Musiikki on selvästi suurin tekijänoikeuskorvausten lähde.

Luvut käyvät ilmi tekijänoikeusjärjestöjen kansainvälisen kattojärjestön CISACin Global Collections Report 2026 -raportista. Raportti tarkastelee musiikin, audiovisuaalisten sisältöjen, visuaalisten taiteiden, kirjallisuuden ja näyttämötaiteen korvauksia. Raportissa on mukana 228 tekijänoikeusjärjestöä kaikkiaan 111 maasta.

title: Holopainen: Jääkiekko on Venäjälle osa valtion propagandaa
content:
Vihreiden kansanedustaja Mari Holopainen pitää Venäjän mahdollista pääsyä takaisin jääkiekon MM-kisoihin erittäin vaarallisena kehityksenä. Urheilun vetoomustuomioistuin CAS näytti Venäjän osallistumiselle vihreää valoa viime perjantaina.

CAS:in päätös ei koske vain Saksan jääkiekon MM-kisoja ensi toukokuussa vaan kaikkia Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliiton MM-turnauksia vuodesta 2027 alkaen. Ensimmäisenä vuorossa on jo vuodenvaihteessa Kanadassa pelattava alle 20-vuotiaiden MM-turnaus.

"Venäjä käy yhä hyökkäyssotaa Ukrainassa. Jääkiekko on Venäjälle paljon enemmän kuin urheilulaji, se on osa valtion propagandaa. On väärin normalisoida hyökkäyssotaa käyvän maan osallistuminen kisoihin", Holopainen sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

Tänään uutisoitiin, että MM-kisojen pitkäaikainen pääsponsori Skoda Auto harkitsee nyt vetäytymistä turnauksen sponsoroinnista. Tähän mennessä useat jääkiekkomaajoukkueet ovat ilmoittaneet vastustavansa Venäjän paluuta. Suomen lisäksi Ruotsi, Tshekki, Norja, Tanska ja Latvia eivät aio pelata Venäjää vastaan.

Holopaisen mukaan vastuu tilanteesta ei saa jäädä liikaa urheilujärjestöjen, kuten Suomen Jääkiekkoliiton ja Kansainvälisen jääkiekkoliitto IIHF:n varaan.

title: Ét år, to domme og intet svar: Kampen om musikken i AI-økonomien
content:
I dag er det et år siden, at musikrettighedsorganisationen Koda sagsøgte den amerikanske AI-musiktjeneste Suno. Det var første gang, at en dansk rettighedsorganisation lagde sag an mod en AI-tjeneste. 

Suno er en platform der lader brugere lave hele sange ud fra en kort tekstbeskrivelse. Ifølge Koda kan tjenesten kun det, fordi den er trænet på eksisterende musik, herunder dansk musik, uden at musikerne er blevet spurgt eller betalt. 

Koda anklager Suno for at have trænet sin AI-model på Kodas repertoire og skjult, hvilke værker der er brugt, og hvordan. I søgsmålet fremlægger Koda eksempler på numre fra Suno, der ligger tæt op ad blandt andet ”Barbie Girl” af Aqua, ”Final Song” af MØ og ”Sleeping My Day Away” af D-A-D.

For Koda er sagen principiel:  

”Først og fremmest er det vigtigt at slå fast, at sagen ikke kun handler om Koda og Suno. Den handler om, hvilke spilleregler vi vil acceptere i AI-økonomien. Hvis tech-giganter frit kan bruge dansk kunst og kultur som gratis råstof til at bygge AI-tjenester, risikerer vi ikke bare at undergrave musikskabernes økonomi, men også selve grundlaget for fremtidens danske kulturliv,” siger Nicky Trebbien, juridisk og politisk direktør i Koda.

title: Diaspora-prosjekter for ytringsfrihet
content:
Fritt Ord støtter høsten 2026 tre ulike diasporaprosjekter: en global medieplattform for ytringsfrihet med base i Norge, to seminarrekker om diasporaers ytringsrom og et nytt arabisk boksenter på Grønland i Oslo. Her kan du se alle ordinære prosjekter som fikk støtte fra Fritt Ord i september og oktober 2026.

Blant dem som får støtte i høst, er den internasjonale medieplattformen Kulna, som skal jobbe med ytringsfrihet og demokrati og dele erfaringer fra kampen mot autoritære regimer med publikum både i Norge og internasjonalt.

Kulna ble lansert i september 2026 og publiserer nå essays, rapporter, podkaster og videoer. Publikum anslås til rundt 750 000 i Midtøsten, USA og Europa – i stor grad eksilmiljøer fra den arabiske verden.
Planen for det første året er 70 podkastepisoder og minst 40 tekster samt videoessays og kortfilmer. På sikt skal Kulna finansieres gjennom abonnement.

title: CFP: Postdigital Archives in Contemporary Literature: (Counter-)Practices and New Challenges in (Digital) Memory
content:
June 23, 2027
Goethe University, Frankfurt

Organization: Anna-Lena Eick (Vrije Universiteit Brussel), Johanna Vollmeyer (Universidad Complutense de Madrid) and Ulrike Mascher (Goethe-Universität Frankfurt) in cooperation with the Frankfurt Memory Studies Platform (FMSP)

Digital technologies have become so pervasive – or in Zara Dinnen’s words “banal” (cf. Dinnen 2018) – that they no longer register as distinct from non-digital aspects of everyday life. This condition, described as “postdigital” (Cramer 2014; Jandrić et al. 2018), is best understood as an interwoven set of cultural shifts that followed the “computerization and global digital networking of communication, technical infrastructures, markets and geopolitics” (cf. Cramer 2014: 13) and likewise affects the epistemic areas of memory and archives. Archives have always been active technologies of governance that produce epistemic order and social hierarchies (Stoler 2009). The postdigital condition raises new questions concerning the archive and memory that cannot be separated from questions of digital infrastructure and mediascape.

title: Beware a Balkan Chinese-Russian Cyber Danger
content:
When Bosnia and Herzegovina held general elections last month, it used biometric voter identification and ballot scanners — a reform widely praised for producing fast and accurate results. That’s a real achievement. But the region’s digital foundations remain fragile, and the region’s adversaries know it.

The Balkan chessboard remains checkered, torn between attraction to the European Union and to Russia, with China maneuvering for leverage. Bosnian nationalists, including separatist, pro-Russian Serbs, won the recent vote. But Serbs gave a pro-European student-led movement a clear majority in another October election, while Montenegro and Albania closed chapters in their EU accession talks. 

The cheapest way to shift the balance of power is to undermine trust in the ballot. For the region, cybersecurity is not a technical issue. It is a strategic one. Washington is waking up to the risk — but needs to increase its focus on digital dangers. The EU is already pressing for action but must also increase its scrutiny.

title: What do Taylor Swift and Giorgia Meloni have in common?
content: Taylor Swift, a billionaire pop empress, and Giorgia Meloni, the far-right Italian prime minister, aren't often mentioned in the same breath. But they're caught in a similar battle, both trying to find new ways to fight an army of AI deepfakes by filing for EU trademarks to protect their voices. Swift's company, TAS Rights Management LLC, wants to register her saying “Hey, it's Taylor Swift”, according to a 6 October filing at the EU Intellectual Property Office. Meloni filed on 5 October to register herself saying “Io sono Giorgia Meloni.” While you can't trademark someone's voice as a whole, these trademarks would give them the exclusive right to their voice saying those words. That could technically stop anyone else from using the voice for a deepfake. Infringing a trademark risks lawsuits and claims for financial damage. It might also be easier to get tech platforms to quickly remove trademark-infringing content. Swift already filed for a US trademark for her voice earlier this year. Earlier this year, I was stuck in hospital for several days, fuzzy on pain medication and bored out of my mind, with nothing but a Steam Deck for company. In the middle of one of those long nights, unable to sleep, I played a game called Titanium Court. It’s a strange creation that looks like it was made for the ZX Spectrum and reads like a postmodern Shakespeare adaptation – a compelling mix of strategy game and match-3 where you rearrange battlefields by matching tiles, before sending tiny lo-fi fairy armies to their deaths.

title: Vermont Has Spent Nearly a Billion Dollars to Clean Up Lake Champlain. But the Green Slime Keeps Coming Back.
content:
On the last day of August, Jeff van den Noort spotted thick swirls of neon green film coating the water just steps from his home in Vermont. He waded in up to his ankles and dipped a jar to get a sample of the scum.

It wasn’t the first time he’d seen the slime. Since his parents bought the house on an island in Lake Champlain in 1966, van den Noort has spent part of nearly every summer in this quiet spot. Back then, the lake was clear.

But he began to witness the water’s deterioration as he grew older, especially after he moved into the home full time in 2010 to care for his ailing mother. That day in late August was the worst he’d seen all summer. 

Later that week, van den Noort grabbed a bucket, a few Mason jars and a smartphone and got into his rusty Saab. He drove past the boat launches, frozen-in-time general stores and windswept pastures of the lake’s islands in northern Vermont and stopped at four other spots along the shore. Each time, he collected some murky water, gauged how thick the muck was, took a few photos and jotted down the weather conditions. He then uploaded his report to an online database.

title: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
content:
No justice for Bangladeshi workers who are recruited into Russia’s war

Originally published on Global Voices

War-wounded Bangladeshis in Russia plead to return home. Screenshot from a YouTube report by Ekhon TV. Fair use.

Maksudur Rahman was 31 when a labor recruiter arrived in his hometown in Lakshmipur district, southeastern Bangladesh, with a job offer: becoming a janitor in Russia. Nearly every family in the district has someone working overseas, so the pitch landed. According to an international investigation, he borrowed money and paid the broker BDT 1.2 million (about USD 9,800). For a household like his, that is a fortune, but the promised wages made the debt look manageable. He signed up and flew out.

title: Speaking in a second language may shift your moral compass – but it can’t overpower it
content:
In today’s interconnected world, millions of people move between two or more languages every day. They may negotiate at work in one language, speak with family in another, and follow news, entertainment and social media across several others.

Using multiple languages can deeply change the way a person sees the world. Research has suggested that thinking and speaking in different languages can fundamentally shift the way we reason and behave, and even change our morality.

Some studies have suggested that using a second language encourages people to make more rational, utilitarian choices, meaning they prioritise the greatest good for the greatest number of people. This is possibly because moral dilemmas feel less emotionally charged when processed in a second language.

But the effect is not cut and dried – other studies have found little or no such effect.

One reason for these mixed findings is that language is only one part of the story. People do not enter a dilemma as a blank slate – they also bring values, past experiences, and sense of self. To date, most research has focused primarily on which language people use, while paying less attention to the person making the decision.

title: Plagiarism is a kind of theft, but it is also a question of honour
content:
Any concept that has a history, philosopher Michel Foucault tells us, cannot have a fixed definition.

Plagiarism is a concept with a history, as the subtitle of Roger Kreuz’s Strikingly Similar: Plagiarism and Appropriation from Chaucer to Chatbots reminds us. But it might be close to perennial.

Review: Strikingly Similar: Plagiarism and Appropriation from Chaucer to Chatbots – Roger Kreuz (Cambridge University Press)

As a term describing literary, artistic or intellectual theft, “plagiarism” is derived from one of the epigrams of the ancient Roman poet Martial:

Quintianus, I commend you my little books – that is, however, if I can call them mine when your poet friend recites them. If they complain of harsh enslavement, come forward to claim their freedom and give bail as required. And when he calls himself their owner, say they are mine, discharged from my hand. If you shout this three or four times, you will make the kidnapper ashamed of himself.
snippet: Any concept that has a history, philosopher Michel Foucault tells us, cannot have a fixed definition.
creator: Benjamin Madden, Senior lecturer, School of Humanities, Adelaide University

title: ‘There Is One Fight’: American Voters Reject Tech Oligarchy
content:
Last month, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Politico that “we believe that the world should accept some bad things happening for the benefits of this technology,” referring to ChatGPT users dying, people losing their jobs to AI, and the other negative externalities we have seen from AI. 

Altman wasn’t running for office Tuesday. But this worldview—that the masses must shut up and suffer while oligarchs centralize power, self-deal, spend wildly to capture the political process, and automate away human endeavors so they can amass yet more wealth—was wholly repudiated in Tuesday’s election as people in Red States, Blue States, and Purple States rejected the cruelty, corruption, and depravity economy we’ve seen over the last few years. They are tired of kleptocracy.

title: Thailand: Halt imminent forcible return of two Uyghur men to China
content:
Responding to reports that two Uyghur men recently moved to an Immigration Detention Centre in Thailand face imminent forcible deportation to China, Amnesty International’s Secretary General Agnès Callamard said:

“Thai authorities must immediately halt any plans to forcibly return these two Uyghur men to China, where they face a real risk of torture, arbitrary detention and enforced disappearance. Thailand must not repeat last year’s unlawful deportation of 40 Uyghurs, who were forced back to danger in China.

“These two men fled persecution only to spend more than a decade detained in Thailand. Amnesty International has documented crimes against humanity against Uyghurs and other predominantly Muslim ethnic groups in Xinjiang. Returning them would expose them to the abuses they sought to escape.

“Both men have previously made clear to their legal representatives that they fear for their lives if returned to China and do not consent to being sent back. Thai authorities must now allow them access to a lawyer of their choice and, together with the international community, urgently find a safe and voluntary third-country solution for them and the other Uyghurs still detained in Thailand.

title: Q&A: What is in the global ‘roadmap’ for transitioning away from fossil fuels?
content:
• Why has Brazil produced a fossil-fuel ‘roadmap’?
  • What does the fossil-fuel roadmap say?
  • How will the fossil-fuel roadmap be discussed at COP31?

    • Transitioning away from fossil fuels is “urgent, inevitable and, yet, possible”, according to a first-of-its-kind global “roadmap” produced by Brazil.

    The host of last year’s climate summit, COP30, has set out a voluntary plan for how countries can move away from coal, oil and gas.

    The roadmap says there is no “one-size-fits-all” approach to transitioning away from fossil fuels and asks countries to “diagnose” their own “readiness” to start the process.

    After mapping out their specific circumstances, countries should then pursue “tailored levers” to take action, according to the roadmap.

    These efforts should culminate by 2033, it says – 10 years on from when the COP28 climate summit in Dubai called on all countries to contribute to a global transition away from fossil fuels.

    Below, Carbon Brief examines what the roadmap says and how it could influence debates about fossil fuels at the upcoming COP31 climate summit, which begins next week in Turkey.

title: "The Earth Shook Last Night": Talarico Wins Senate, Hinojosa Becomes First Latina Governor in Texas
content:
Texas Democrats have shattered more than three decades of Republican dominance in the state, winning races for U.S. Senate, governor, lieutenant governor, attorney general and even railroad commissioner. They are also poised to possibly take control of the Texas House of Representatives for the first time since 2003. The Republican governor of Texas, Greg Abbott, lost his bid for a fourth term to Democratic state Representative Gina Hinojosa, who defeated him by nearly 700,000 votes. She will be Texas’s first Latina governor. And James Talarico will be the first Democrat to represent Texas in the U.S. Senate since 1993.

“We’re celebrating these wonderful candidates who won office, and we’re also starting to think about what it means to hold power,” says Mike Siegel, a city council member from Austin, Texas, who founded Ground Game Texas, a statewide voter turnout organization. “We need to start thinking very quickly about how we will protect public education, how we will stop data centers and the encroachment of AI on our society, how we will protect public schools, how we stop collaboration with ICE.”

title: Kasvatusalan ammattilaisilla hyvät mahdollisuudet edistää väestön liikkumista – koulutus ei vielä anna siihen riittäviä valmiuksia
content:
Valtaosa väestöstä ei täytä liikkumissuosituksia ja liikkuu terveytensä kannalta liian vähän. Väestön liikkumisen edistämiseksi tarvitaan mukaan kaikki hallinnonalat. Erityisesti mukaan tarvitaan koulutuspolitiikka, jotta kasvatus- ja opetusammattilaiset osaisivat omassa työssään edistää liikkumista ja liikuntaa.

Valtion liikuntaneuvoston tilaaman selvityksen mukaan liikkuminen on tunnistettavissa useimmissa tarkastelluissa kasvatusalan koulutuksissa, mutta liikkuminen muodostaa vain harvoin kaikille opiskelijoille yhteisen, koulutuksen eri osiin ulottuvan osaamisalueen. Liikkuminen keskittyy usein yksittäiseen opintojaksoon tai valinnaiseen kokonaisuuteen tai jää opetuksen käytännön toteutustavaksi.

Selvityksen kyselyyn vastanneet kasvatusalan ammattilaiset pitävät ammattialan roolia merkittävänä liikkumiseen ohjaamisessa. Vastaajat myös toivovat liikkumisen näkyvän tutkinnon tavoitteissa ja tai sisällöissä nykyistä enemmän. Kasvatusalan koulutuksissa on jo runsaasti sisältöjä ja tavoitteita, joihin liikkuminen voidaan luontevasti kiinnittää nykyistä vahvemmin.
